question_content: pA DevOps engineer administers an application that manages video files for a video production company. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an ELB Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Data is stored in an Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance, and the video files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. On a typical day, 50 GB of new video are added to the S3 bucket. The engineer must implement a multi-Region disaster recovery plan with the least data loss and the lowest recovery times. The current application infrastructure is already described using AWS CloudFormation.pWhich deployment option should the engineer choose to meet the uptime and recovery objectives for the system?

answer_choices.choice_content: pLaunch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second Region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Create an Amazon RDS read replica in the second Region. In the second Region, enable Cross-Region Replication between the original S3 bucket and a new S3 bucket. To fail over, promote the read replica as primary. Update the CloudFormation stack and increase the capacity of the Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This deployment option results in the least amount of lost data and the lowest recovery times because it uses ongoing replication for the data in Amazon S3 and the data in Amazon RDS. The use of CloudFormation provides an identical setup in the failover Region with one instance that is ready to receive traffic. For data, S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) asynchronously copies changes that are made to the original S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket in the failover Region. In Amazon RDS, there is asynchronous replication of data and changes to the read replica in the failover Region.pFor more information about read replicas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html"Working with Read Replicas/a/span.pFor more information about S3 CRR, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html"Replicating Objects/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLaunch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second Region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Create a scheduled task to take daily Amazon RDS cross-Region snapshots to the second Region. In the second Region, enable Cross-Region Replication between the original S3 bucket and Amazon S3 Glacier. In a disaster, launch a new application stack in the second Region and restore the database from the most recent snapshot.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In the event of a failure, S3 Glacier might be unavailable in the Region. In such a situation, you would not be able to restore the database or the S3 bucket. A daily task to replicate snapshots would provide resiliency, but the data loss and time to recover would be greater than for ongoing replication to an instance in the failover Region. This deployment option would not provide the lowest recovery times or the least amount of data loss.pFor more information about snapshot copying, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html"Copying a DB Snapshot/a/span.pFor more information about resilience in S3 Glacier, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html"Resilience in Amazon S3 Glacier/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLaunch the application from the CloudFormation template in the second Region, which sets the capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 1. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a nightly task to take a snapshot of the database, copy the snapshot to the second Region, and replace the DB instance in the second Region from the snapshot. In the second Region, enable Cross-Region Replication between the original S3 bucket and a new S3 bucket. To fail over, increase the capacity of the Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In the event of a failure, a daily task to take snapshots would provide resiliency. However, the data loss and time to recover would be greater than for ongoing replication to an instance in the failover Region. This deployment option would not provide the lowest recovery times or the least amount of data loss.pFor more information about snapshot copying, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html"Copying a DB Snapshot/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon EventBridge to schedule a nightly task to take a snapshot of the database and copy the snapshot to the second Region. Create an AWS Lambda function that copies each object to a new S3 bucket in the second Region in response to S3 event notifications. In the second Region, launch the application from the CloudFormation template and restore the database from the most recent snapshot.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In the event of a failure, a daily task to take snapshots would provide resiliency. However, the data loss and time to recover would be greater than for ongoing replication to an instance in the failover Region. This deployment option would not provide the lowest recovery times or the least amount of data loss. Additionally, the use of a Lambda function to copy each object is inefficient in time and cost. This solution could miss other types of changes made to objects, such as deletions, and would negatively impact the RPO and RTO.pFor more information about snapshot copying, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_CopySnapshot.html"Copying a DB Snapshot/a/span.

question_content: pA company is beginning to move to the AWS Cloud. Internal customers are classified into two groups according to their AWS skills: beginners and experts.pThe DevOps engineer needs to build a solution to allow beginners to deploy a restricted set of AWS architecture blueprints expressed as AWS CloudFormation templates. Deployment should only be possible on predetermined Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs). However, expert users should be able to deploy blueprints without constraints. Experts should also be able to access other AWS services, as needed.pHow can the engineer implement a solution to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pApply constraints to the parameters in the templates, limiting the VPCs available for deployments. Store the templates on Amazon S3. Create an IAM group for beginners and give them access to the templates and CloudFormation. Create a separate group for experts, giving them access to the templates, CloudFormation, and other AWS services.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter constraints would restrict the experts and would limit the available VPCs to the VPCs within the Parameters AllowedValues property. This solution does not meet the requirement to allow the experts to create AWS resources without constraints.pFor more information about parameters in CloudFormation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuidearameters-section-structure.html"Parameters/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore the templates on Amazon S3. Use AWS Service Catalog to create a portfolio of products based on those templates. Apply template constraints to the products with rules limiting VPCs available for deployments. Create an IAM group for beginners giving them access to the portfolio. Create a separate group for experts giving them access to the templates, CloudFormation, and other AWS services.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The use of template constraints at the AWS Service Catalog level minimizes overhead, provides constrained access to the templates for beginners, and provides unconstrained access for experts. Beginners will deploy by using the AWS Service Catalog products with template constraints. Experts will deploy directly by using CloudFormation with no constraints.pFor more information about AWS Service Catalog template constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/catalogs_constraints_template-constraints.html"AWS Service Catalog Template Constraints/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore the templates on Amazon S3. Use AWS Service Catalog to create a portfolio of products based on those templates. Create an IAM role restricting VPCs available for creation of AWS resources. Apply a launch constraint to the products using this role. Create an IAM group for beginners giving them access to the portfolio. Create a separate group for experts giving them access to the portfolio and other AWS services.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With this solution, experts would have access to only the AWS Service Catalog portfolio and could not deploy the CloudFormation templates without constraints. A launch constraint specifies the IAM role that AWS Service Catalog assumes when an end user launches, updates, or terminates a product. The use of IAM groups has no effect when a launch constraint with an IAM role is applied for an AWS Service Catalog product to create AWS resources in the template.pFor more information about AWS Service Catalog launch constraints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-launch.html"AWS Service Catalog Launch Constraints/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate two templates for each architecture blueprint where only one of them limits the VPCs available for deployments. Store the templates in Amazon DynamoDB. Create an IAM group for beginners giving them access to the constrained templates and CloudFormation. Create a separate group for experts giving them access to the unconstrained templates, CloudFormation, and other AWS services.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudFormation does not directly support the use of DynamoDB as a source for the template. With CloudFormation, you can provide the template in the body or store the template in an S3 bucket and provide the S3 URL. Additionally, the use of two sets of templates is not optimal and does not meet the requirement for the least amount of overhead.pFor more information about CloudFormation template size, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cloudformation-limits.html"AWS CloudFormation Quotas/a/span.pFor more information about how CloudFormation consumes templates from local machines or Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-whatis-howdoesitwork.html"How Does AWS CloudFormation Work?/a/span

question_content: pA DevOps engineer is deploying an AWS Service Catalog portfolio using AWS CodePipeline. The pipeline should create products and templates based on a manifest file in either JSON or YAML, and should enforce security requirements on all AWS Service Catalog products managed through the pipeline.pWhich solution will meet the requirements in an automated fashion?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Service Catalog deploy action in AWS CodeDeploy to push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog with verification steps in the CodeDeploy AppSpec.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AWS Service Catalog deploy action does not exist in CodeDeploy. CodeDeploy is a deployment service that automates application deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises instances, serverless AWS Lambda functions, or Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services.pFor more information about CodeDeploy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is CodeDeploy/a/spana target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html"?/a

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Service Catalog deploy action in AWS CodeBuild to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AWS Service Catalog deploy action does not exist in CodeBuild. CodeBuild compiles source code and produces artifacts that are ready to deploy. You must add custom logic within CodeBuild to invoke other AWS services.pFor more information about CodeBuild, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is AWS CodeBuild?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Lambda action in CodePipeline to run a Lambda function to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can add a Lambda function as an action in CodePipeline. The Lambda function can verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog by invoking the Service Catalog API.pFor more information about how to invoke a Lambda function in a CodePipeline pipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-invoke-lambda-function.html"Invoke an AWS Lambda Function in a Pipeline in CodePipeline/a/span.pFor more information about Service Catalog API operations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/dg/service-catalog-api-overview.html#product-management"Products/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Lambda action in AWS CodeBuild to run a Lambda function to verify and push new versions of products into the AWS Service Catalog.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeBuild does not natively integrate with Lambda. You must add custom logic within CodeBuild to invoke other AWS services.pFor more information about how to use Lambda with other services, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-services.html"Using AWS Lambda with Other Services/a/span.

question_content: pA company wants to migrate a legacy application to AWS and develop a deployment pipeline that uses AWS services only. A DevOps engineer is migrating all of the application code from a Git repository to AWS CodeCommit while preserving the history of the repository. The DevOps engineer has set all the permissions within CodeCommit, installed the Git client and the AWS CLI on a local computer, and is ready to migrate the repository.pWhich actions will follow?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate the CodeCommit repository using the AWS CLI. Clone the Git repository directly to CodeCommit using the AWS CLI. Validate that the files were migrated, and publish the CodeCommit repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot directly clone the Git repository to CodeCommit. You must first clone the Git repository to the local computer with the --mirror option to clone a bare copy of the remote repository.pFor more information about how to clone a repository and how to push to a CodeCommit repository, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-migrate-repository-existing.html#how-to-migrate-existing-clone"Step 2: Clone the Repository and Push to the CodeCommit Repository/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console. Clone both the Git and CodeCommit repositories to the local computer. Copy the files from the Git repository to the CodeCommit repository on the local computer. Commit the CodeCommit repository. Validate that the files were migrated, and share the CodeCommit repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You do not have to clone the CodeCommit repository to the local computer. You should clone only the Git repository to the local computer with the --mirror option. Then you should push the Git repository to CodeCommit.pFor more information about how to clone a repository and how to push to a CodeCommit repository, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-migrate-repository-existing.html#how-to-migrate-existing-clone"Step 2: Clone the Repository and Push to the CodeCommit Repository/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console. Use the console to clone the Git repository into the CodeCommit repository. Validate that the files were migrated, and publish the CodeCommit repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You must first clone the Git repository to the local computer with the --mirror option to clone a bare copy of the remote repository. Additionally, CodeCommit does not integrate with any service to clone Git repositories into CodeCommit through the console.pFor more information about how to clone a repository and how to push to a CodeCommit repository, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-migrate-repository-existing.html#how-to-migrate-existing-clone"Step 2: Clone the Repository and Push to the CodeCommit Repository/a/span.pFor more information about service integrations with CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/integrations.html"Product and Service Integrations with AWS CodeCommit/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate the CodeCommit repository using the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. Clone the Git repository with a mirror argument to the local computer and push the repository to CodeCommit. Validate that the files were migrated, and share the CodeCommit repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution meets the requirements to migrate the Git repository to CodeCommit while preserving the history of the repository.pFor more information about how to migrate a Git repository to CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-migrate-repository-existing.html"Migrate a Git Repository to AWS CodeCommit/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access its AWS accounts. The company manages the AWS accounts with AWS Organizations. In the central network account, the company recently created a transit gateway to handle routing between all AWS accounts. The company wants to use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the transit gateway with the company's current and future AWS accounts.pWhat should a DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pWithin the organization's management account, activate AWS RAM for trusted access and create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the central network account as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You should create the resource share from the central network account because that account is where the transit gateway exists. You should share the transit gateway with other accounts in the organization by providing the organization ID, not the central network account, as the principal within AWS RAM.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWithin the central network account, activate organizational sharing in AWS RAM and create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the organization ID as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You must first enable resource sharing from within the organization's management account, not the central network account. The transit gateway exists in the central network account.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWithin the organization's management account, activate AWS RAM for trusted access. Within the central network account, create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the organization ID as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Within the organization's management account, you can enable resource sharing at the organization level. You can create a resource share by using AWS RAM in the same account that contains the resource that you need to share. In this case, that account is the central network account that has the transit gateway. When you share the transit gateway within AWS RAM, provide the organization ID as the principal. After you add an organization or an OU to a resource share, changes to the accounts that are in an OU or accounts that join or leave the organization dynamically affect the resource share. For example, if you add a new account to an OU that has access to a resource share, then the new member account automatically receives access to the shared resources.pFor more information about how to share resources within Organizations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html#getting-started-sharing-orgs"Enable Resource Sharing within AWS Organizations/a/span.pFor more information about how to create a resource share, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html#getting-started-sharing-create"Create a Resource Share/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWithin the central network account, activate organizational sharing in AWS RAM. Within the organization's management account, create a resource share with a resource type of Transit Gateway. Select the existing transit gateway as the resource. Specify the central network account as the principal.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You must first enable resource sharing from within the organization's management account, not the central network account. The transit gateway exists in the central network account. You should share the transit gateway with all the accounts in the organization by providing the organization ID, not the central network account, as the principal within AWS RAM.

question_content: pA DevOps engineer wants to implement an automated response that will occur if AWS Trusted Advisor detects an IAM access key in a public source code repository. The automated response must delete the exposed access key and must notify the security team.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function to delete the IAM access key. Configure AWS CloudTrail logs to stream to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter for the AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED event with two actions. First, run the Lambda function. Second, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send a notification to the security team.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution uses the AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED event, which originates from the AWS Health Dashboard. However, the requirement in the scenario is to monitor Trusted Advisor. This solution does not meet that requirement.pFor more information about CloudTrail events, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-concepts.html#cloudtrail-concepts-events" target="_blank"What Are CloudTrail Events?/a/spanpFor more information about the Trusted Advisor check for exposed access keys, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html#exposed-access-keys" target="_blank"Exposed Access Keys/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function to delete the IAM access key. Create an AWS Config rule for changes to "aws.trustedadvisor" and the "Exposed Access Keys" status with two actions. First, run the Lambda function. Second, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send a notification to the security team.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot configure an AWS Config rule to monitor changes to Trusted Advisor.pFor more information about supported resource types for AWS Config, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/resource-config-reference.html"Supported Resource Types/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function that deletes the IAM access key and then uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the security team. Create an AWS Health Dashboard rule for the AWS_RISK_CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED event. Set the target of the Health Dashboard rule to the ARN of the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Health Dashboard does not provide native rule functionality or targets. Nothing would invoke the Lambda function, so no notifications would be sent.pFor more information about the AWS Health Dashboard, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/getting-started-health-dashboard.html" target="_blank"Getting Started with Your AWS Health Dashboard – Your Account Health/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function that deletes the IAM access key. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an "aws.trustedadvisor" event source and the "Exposed Access Keys" status. Set the EventBridge rule to target the Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that notifies the security team.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use EventBridge to create a rule that has Trusted Advisor as the event source. The rule can target a Lambda function to delete the IAM access key and can target an SNS topic to provide the notification.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to monitor Trusted Advisor, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cloudwatch-events-ta.html"Monitoring AWS Trusted Advisor Check Results with Amazon EventBridge/a/span.pFor more information about available Trusted Advisor checks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor-check-reference.html"AWS Trusted Advisor Check Reference/a/span.pFor more information about the Trusted Advisor check for exposed access keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html#exposed-access-keys"Exposed Access Keys/a/span.pFor more information about Trusted Advisor metrics and dimensions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cloudwatch-metrics-ta.html#trusted-advisor-metrics-dimensions"Trusted Advisor Metrics and Dimensions/a/span.

question_content: pA company hosts an application in North America. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. A team of analysts in Europe generates real-time reports by using the DB cluster. The analysts must have access to the most up-to-date data. A DevOps engineer discovers that the generation of reports is much slower for users in Europe than for users in North America.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do to resolve this issue?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon DynamoDB table in Europe. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to configure replication between the DB cluster and the DynamoDB table. Configure the users' machines to point to the DynamoDB table in Europe.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DAX is designed for scale and performance, but DAX is not designed for replication between different databases.pFor more information about DAX, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html"In-Memory Acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate cross-Region Aurora Replicas in North America, and activate synchronous replication. Configure the users' machines to point to the Aurora reader endpoint in North America.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Aurora Replicas are within a single Region. To perform multi-Region replication, you must use an Aurora global database.pFor more information about Aurora Replicas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html"Replication with Amazon Aurora/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Aurora global database. Use the existing DB cluster as the primary cluster, and add a secondary cluster in an AWS Region in Europe. Configure the users' machines to point to the Aurora reader endpoint in Europe.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. With an Aurora global database, you can run globally distributed applications by using a single Aurora database that crosses multiple Regions.pFor more information about Aurora global databases, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html"Using Amazon Aurora Global Databases/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon DynamoDB global tables in an AWS Region in Europe. Set up continuous replication between the DB cluster and the DynamoDB table by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Configure the users' machines to point to the DynamoDB table in Europe.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DynamoDB global tables provide a fully managed solution for deploying a multi-Region, multi-active database. DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, and the application in the scenario is using a PostgreSQL DB cluster. This solution would require you to rebuild the entire database or duplicate the database across two database solutions.pFor more information about DynamoDB global tables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html"Global Tables - Multi-Region Replication for DynamoDB/a/span.

question_content: pA company must collect user consent to a privacy agreement. The company deploys an application in six AWS Regions: two Regions in North America, two Regions in Europe, and two Regions in Asia. The application has a user base of 20 million to 30 million users.pThe company needs to read and write data that is related to each user's response. The company also must ensure that the responses are available in all six Regions.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST latency of reads and writes?

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) in each of the six Regions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although Amazon DocumentDB provides a global cluster feature, this solution does not meet the requirement for lowest latency on writes. An Amazon DocumentDB global cluster consists of one primary Region and up to five read-only secondary Regions. The write operations in the scenario are directed to one of six Regions. The result is an increase in write latency for the users that are not in that specific Region.pFor more information about Amazon DocumentDB global clusters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/global-clusters.html"Overview of Amazon DocumentDB Global Clusters/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement Amazon DynamoDB global tables in each of the six Regions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. DynamoDB global tables provide a fully managed, multi-Region, and multi-active database that guarantees the lowest read and write latency. With global tables, the application puts data in the table of the user's Region. DynamoDB then replicates the data automatically across Regions.pFor more information about DynamoDB global tables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html#GlobalTablesOverview"Replicate Data Seamlessly across Regions with Global Tables/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement Amazon ElastiCache for Redis replication groups in each of the six Regions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Global Datastore for Redis feature can work with fully managed replication across Regions. However, this solution does not meet the requirement for lowest latency on writes. With this feature, Redis provides a primary cluster that accepts read and writes, and a secondary cluster that accepts only read requests. Therefore, the write operations in the scenario are directed to one of six Regions. The result is an increase in write latency for the users that are not in that specific Region. Additionally, this feature supports a maximum of two secondary clusters. The company in the scenario needs six clusters.pFor more information about the Global Datastore for Redis feature, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Redis-Global-Datastore.html"Replication across AWS Regions Using Global Datastores/a/span.pFor more information about limitations of the Global Datastore feature, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Redis-Global-Datastores-Getting-Started.html"Prerequisites and Limitations/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement Amazon OpenSearch Service in each of the six Regions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With cross-cluster replication in OpenSearch Service, you can replicate indexes, mappings, and metadata from one OpenSearch Service domain to another. The replication follows an active-passive replication model where the follower index pulls data from the leader index. In this configuration, the write operations are directed to the leader domain that resides in one of the six Regions. The result is an increase in write latency for the users that are not in that specific Region.pFor more information about cross-cluster replication in OpenSearch Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/replication.html"Cross-Cluster Replication for Amazon OpenSearch Service/a/span.

question_content: pA company's legacy application uses IAM user credentials to access resources in the company's AWS Organizations organization. A DevOps engineer must ensure that new IAM users cannot be created unless the employee who creates the IAM user is on an exception list.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAttach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateAccessKey actions with a condition that excludes StringEquals for aws:username with a value of the exception list.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would allow the creation of new users, regardless of the exception status. This solution would also deny the CreateAccessKey action for pre-existing users if they are not on the exception list.pFor more information about SCP rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_strategies.html"Strategies for Using SCPs/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAttach an Organizations SCP with an explicit deny for all iam:CreateUser actions with a condition that includes StringNotLike for aws:username with a value of the exception list.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use an SCP to deny the CreateUser action while specifying conditions such as approved user names.pFor more information about IAM policy elements, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition.html"IAM JSON Policy Elements: Condition/a/span.pFor more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_examples.html#example-scp-restricts-with-exception"Example Service Control Policies/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateAccessKey action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would prevent existing users from rotating their credentials. However, this solution would not prevent the creation of console users.pFor more information about IAM actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_Operations.html"Actions/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule with a pattern that matches the iam:CreateUser action with an AWS Lambda function target. The function will check the user name and account against an exception list. If the user is not on the exception list, the function will delete the user.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In this solution, the Lambda function will delete the new user if the employee who created the user is not on the exception list. However, this solution still would allow an employee who is not on the exception list to create the user. The scenario requirements state that the user cannot be created if the employee is not on the exception list.pFor more information about IAM actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/APIReference/API_Operations.html"Actions/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses federated access for its AWS environment. The company creates and manages IAM roles by using AWS CloudFormation from a CI/CD pipeline. All changes should be made to the IAM roles through the pipeline.pThe company's security team discovers that out-of-band changes are being made to the IAM roles. The security team needs a way to detect when these out-of-band changes occur.pWhat should a DevOps engineer do to meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Inspector rules to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack has a configuration change.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Inspector does not detect and notify when a CloudFormation stack has a configuration change. Amazon Inspector scans AWS workloads for vulnerabilities and scans Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.pFor more information about Amazon Inspector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html"What Is Amazon Inspector?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Trusted Advisor to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack has a configuration change.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Trusted Advisor can inspect the AWS environment and provide recommendations to save money, improve system availability and performance, and help close security gaps. However, Trusted Advisor does not have a security check for configuration changes in CloudFormation.pFor more information about Trusted Advisor, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html"AWS Trusted Advisor/a/span.pFor more information about security checks in Trusted Advisor, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html"Security/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudTrail to detect and notify when an AWS CloudFormation stack detects a configuration change.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudTrail can record when activity occurs in CloudFormation, but CloudTrail cannot notify.pFor more information about CloudFormation information in CloudTrail, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/cfn-api-logging-cloudtrail.html"Logging AWS CloudFormation API Calls with AWS CloudTrail/a/span.pFor more information about CloudTrail, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-user-guide.html"What Is AWS CloudTrail?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Config rule to detect and notify when AWS CloudFormation drift detection identifies a configuration change.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check AWS Config managed rule checks whether the actual configuration of a CloudFormation stack differs, or has drifted, from the expected configuration.pFor more information about the cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check AWS Config managed rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check.html"cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check/a/span.

question_content: pAn ecommerce company is running an application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The database layer is hosted on an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Amazon Route 53 DNS records point to the ALB.pThe company needs to create a standby disaster recovery solution in an additional AWS Region. The company cannot make any changes to the application code.pWhich combination of actions will meet these requirements with the LOWEST cost? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a failover routing policy for the application DNS entry.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. To create an active-passive failover configuration with one primary record and one secondary record, you must create the records and specify a failover routing policy.pFor more information about failover routing, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html#dns-failover-types-active-passive"Active-Passive Failover/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a geolocation routing policy for the application DNS entry.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A geolocation routing policy provides routing based on where the request is originating, not for failover between resources.pFor more information about geolocation routing policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-geo.html"Geolocation Routing/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a cross-Region read replica of the DB instance in the new standby Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. When backup replication is configured for a DB instance, Amazon RDS initiates a cross-Region copy of all snapshots and transaction logs as soon as they are ready on the DB instance.pFor more information about cross-Region replication for Amazon RDS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReplicateBackups.html"Replicating Automated Backups to Another AWS Region/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMigrate the database layer to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure global replication to the new standby Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The scenario states that the company cannot make changes to the application. A migration to DynamoDB would require application changes.pFor more information about DynamoDB global replication, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html"Global Tables - Multi-Region Replication for DynamoDB/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pProvision the ALB and the Auto Scaling group in the new standby Region. Set the desired capacity to match the desired capacity in the active Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This action would be equivalent to running an active-active recovery process and would not result in the lowest cost.pFor more information about backup and recovery options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html"Disaster Recovery Options in the Cloud/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pProvision the ALB and the Auto Scaling group in the new standby Region. Set the desired capacity to 1.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This action is a pilot light active-passive configuration and meets the scenario's requirements with the lowest cost.pFor more information about backup and recovery options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html"Disaster Recovery Options in the Cloud/a/span.

question_content: pA company has a single-page application that was developed in Angular. A DevOps engineer needs to automate deployments of the application to a website that the company hosts on Amazon S3. The solution must provide version control of the source code and must give developers the ability to perform peer review.pWhich combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS CodeCommit repository to store the source code. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that has a source of the CodeCommit repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeCommit provides version control of the source code and gives developers the ability to perform peer review. CodePipeline also can automate deployments of the application. The CodePipeline pipeline can be invoked when changes are pushed to the CodeCommit repository.pFor more information about CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is AWS CodeCommit?/a/spanpFor more information about CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is AWS CodePipeline?/a/spanpFor more information about how to use pull requests to review changes in CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguideull-requests.html"Working with Pull Requests in AWS CodeCommit Repositories/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an S3 bucket to act as the source for developers to upload their source code. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that has the S3 bucket as the source.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an S3 bucket as a source location for a source action of a CodePipeline pipeline. An S3 bucket can provide version control, but an S3 bucket does not provide the ability to use pull requests for peer review.pFor more information about Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html"What Is Amazon S3?/a/spanpFor more information about the S3 source action of a CodePipeline pipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-S3.html"Amazon S3 Source Action/a/span.pFor more information about S3 Versioning, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Versioning.html"Using Versioning in S3 Buckets/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the AWS CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS CodeBuild phase that compiles the source code and produces build artifacts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeBuild can compile source code and can produce artifacts that are ready to deploy through CodePipeline.pFor more information about CodeBuild, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is AWS CodeBuild?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the AWS CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS CodeDeploy phase that compiles the source code, produces build artifacts, and then deploys the website.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy cannot compile source code. CodeDeploy is a deployment service that automates application deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises instances, serverless AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services.pFor more information about CodeDeploy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is CodeDeploy?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the AWS CodePipeline pipeline, configure an AWS AppConfig deploy action that deploys the build artifacts to the S3 website bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS AppConfig, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, cannot deploy to Amazon S3. AWS AppConfig deploys application configurations to applications that are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Lambda functions, containers, mobile applications, or IoT devices.pFor more information about AWS AppConfig, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appconfig/latest/userguide/what-is-appconfig.html"What Is AWS AppConfig?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the AWS CodePipeline pipeline, configure an S3 deploy action that deploys the build artifacts to the S3 website bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can add an action that uses Amazon S3 as a deployment provider to the CodePipeline pipeline.pFor more information about the S3 deploy action of a CodePipeline pipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-S3Deploy.html"Amazon S3 Deploy Action/a/span.

question_content: pA company grants external users access to its AWS account by creating an IAM user for each external user. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution to revoke access from IAM users that have not accessed the account in 90 days.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pTurn on AWS Config in the AWS account. Deploy the iam-user-unused-credentials-check AWS Config managed rule. Configure the rule to run periodically. Configure AWS Config automatic remediation to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Config can assess, audit, and evaluate configurations of resources. The iam-user-unused-credentials-check AWS Config managed rule can check whether IAM users have passwords or active access keys that have not been used within a specified number of days. Additionally, the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials runbook revokes unused IAM passwords and active access keys.pFor more information about AWS Config, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html"What Is AWS Config?/a/spanpFor more information about the iam-user-unused-credentials-check AWS Config managed rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/iam-user-unused-credentials-check.html"iam-user-unused-credentials-check/a/span.pFor more information about the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials runbook, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-aws-revoke-iam-user.html"AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to create an analyzer in the AWS account. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match IAM Access Analyzer events for IAM users that were last accessed more than 90 days ago. Configure the rule to run the AWSConfigRemediation-DetachIAMPolicy AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to detach any policies that are attached to the IAM user.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources that are shared with external principals. However, IAM Access Analyzer does not monitor whether IAM users have accessed the account in a specified number of days.pFor more information about IAM Access Analyzer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html"Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable AWS Trusted Advisor in the AWS account. Use the AWS Developer Support plan to access the AWS Support API. Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to use the Support API's Trusted Advisor IAM Access Key Rotation check to discover IAM credentials that have not been accessed for more than 90 days. Configure another EventBridge rule to use the Trusted Advisor Check Item Refresh Status event type and to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Trusted Advisor can inspect the AWS environment and provide recommendations to save money, improve system availability and performance, and help close security gaps. One of the Trusted Advisor security checks is IAM Access Key Rotation, which checks for active IAM access keys that have not been rotated in the last 90 days. However, the AWS Developer Support plan does not give access to the AWS Support API. Only the AWS Business Support plan, AWS Enterprise On-Ramp Support plan, and AWS Enterprise Support plan provide access to the AWS Support API.pFor more information about Trusted Advisor and the AWS Support API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html"AWS Trusted Advisor/a/span.pFor more information about the IAM Access Key Rotation security check, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/security-checks.html#iam-access-key-rotation"IAM Access Key Rotation/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable AWS Security Hub in the AWS account. Configure a Security Hub rule that determines when an IAM user was last accessed. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match the Security Hub rule and to run the AWSConfigRemediation-RevokeUnusedIAMUserCredentials AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Security Hub recommends that you turn on resource recording in AWS Config before you enable Security Hub standards. Additionally, you would need an AWS Config rule to identify IAM users that have not accessed the account in 90 days.pFor more information about how to enable and configure AWS Config, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-prereq-config.html"Enabling and Configuring AWS Config/a/span.pFor more information about how Security Hub uses AWS Config rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-standards-awsconfigrules.html"How Security Hub Uses AWS Config Rules to Run Security Checks/a/span.

question_content: pA company has 50 AWS accounts and plans to add another 20 accounts in the next few months. The company needs to enable AWS Config and Amazon GuardDuty in all the existing accounts and is planning to use AWS Organizations. The company needs a solution that will enable AWS Config and GuardDuty in new accounts as soon as the accounts are created. Users in the accounts must not have the ability to make any changes to these services.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDelegate AWS Firewall Manager to a dedicated security account in the organization. Set up Firewall Manager in the security account. Configure a policy to enable AWS Config and GuardDuty. Deploy the policy to all accounts. Set up a new IAM role that denies changes to AWS Config and GuardDuty.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Firewall Manager does not support the automation that is needed in the newly created AWS accounts. In addition, Firewall Manager does not support AWS Config or GuardDuty.pFor more information about Firewall Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-chapter.html"AWS Firewall Manager/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS CloudFormation template that enables AWS Config and GuardDuty. Deploy the CloudFormation template across the organization from a delegated administrator account by using CloudFormation StackSets. In the organization's management account, create an SCP that denies changes to AWS Config and GuardDuty.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CloudFormation StackSets can deploy the necessary services in the newly created AWS accounts. An SCP will deny any future changes.pFor more information about available service integrations with CloudFormation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-cloudformation.html"AWS CloudFormation StackSets and AWS Organizations/a/span.pFor more information about SCPs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"Service Control Policies (SCPs)/a/span.pFor more information about how to manage multiple accounts in GuardDuty, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_accounts.html"Managing Multiple Accounts in Amazon GuardDuty/a/span.pFor more information about how to register a delegated administrator for CloudFormation StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-delegated-admin.html"Register a Delegated Administrator/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to deploy AWS Config and GuardDuty through AWS CloudFormation StackSets. In the organization's management account, create an IAM policy that denies changes to AWS Config and GuardDuty.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. To prevent changes from occurring in all accounts in the organization, you should use SCPs instead of IAM policies.pFor more information about the differences between SCPs and IAM policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html#scp-effects-on-permissions"SCP Effects on Permissions/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule in each account to invoke an AWS Lambda function each hour. Configure the function to check whether AWS Config and GuardDuty are enabled and to enable these services if they are not enabled. In each account, create an IAM policy that denies changes to AWS Config and GuardDuty. Attach the policy to the existing users and roles in the accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution could work for the existing AWS accounts, but this solution would not work for the newly created AWS accounts. The EventBridge rule would invoke the Lambda function once an hour. Therefore, if any remediation action needed to occur, the action would not occur immediately. In addition, new users or groups would not have the necessary Deny policy attached.pFor more information about EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is.html"What Is Amazon EventBridge?/a/span

question_content: pA company is running two applications: application-a and application-b. The applications run on separate Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux. The instances for application-a and application-b are in the same VPC and are spread across multiple Availability Zones. The application-a instances run in different Availability Zones than the application-b instances. Each instance is associated with an IAM role that is based on the application that the instance hosts.pA development team needs to allow application-a to have read/write access to all data in a storage solution. The development team must allow application-b to have read/write access to only the /data/application-b directory.pThe development team deploys an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with mount targets in each Availability Zone. The EFS file system is already mounted on the application-a instances. A DevOps engineer must complete the configuration.pWhich combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), create a resource share for the EFS file system. Share the file system with IAM roles for application-a and application-b.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With AWS RAM, you can share resources that are created and managed by other AWS services. Therefore, you cannot use AWS RAM to share EFS resources.pFor more information about which resources you can share by using AWS RAM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html"Shareable AWS Resources/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an EFS access point for application-b with the root directory path of /data/application-b. Set the root directory creation permissions to 0755.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An EFS access point can provide application-b with read/write access to the file system.pFor more information about EFS access points, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/efs-access-points.html"Working with Amazon EFS Access Points/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFor application-b, configure the file system policy to allow the instance role used for application-b to mount and write to the file system. Include a condition statement to ensure that the application role can access the file system through only the access point.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. With Amazon EFS, you can configure least privilege access by using an IAM resource policy (also referred to as an EFS file system policy) and access points. Access points are application-specific entry points to the EFS file system and provide clients with access to a specific directory or subdirectory on the file system. You use the file system policy to grant permissions to clients, which are identified by IAM roles.pFor more information about how to use IAM policies to control access, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/iam-access-control-nfs-efs.html"Using IAM to Control File System Data Access/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFor each application, create an additional EFS mount target in each Availability Zone. Configure the mount target policy to allow the role for the application to mount and write to the file system. Include a condition statement to ensure that the application role can access the file system through only the access point.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon EFS does not support policy configuration for mount targets and does not support multiple mount targets in a single Availability Zone. If application-a and application-b try to scale with multiple replications in a single Availability Zone, this configuration will act as a limitation.pFor more information about EFS mount targets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/accessing-fs.html"Creating and Managing Mount Targets and Security Groups/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pOn each EC2 instance, create a user for the application that the instance is running. Ensure that each user has a unique user ID and group ID. Mount the file system by using the user account. Change the ownership of the mount directory path to correspond to the application.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There are several options for mounting an EFS file system. However, user account is not a valid option.pFor more information about how to mount EFS file systems, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/mounting-fs.html"Mounting EFS File Systems/a/span.

question_content: pA large company has acquired a small company. The large company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The large company needs to integrate the small company's single AWS account into the organization with minimal impact to the applications that are deployed in the small company's account.pThe large company has deployed AWS Control Tower in its organization and wants to enroll the small company's account in AWS Control Tower. The large company's AWS Control Tower configuration includes a security OU, a sandbox OU, and a new destination OU that is set up for the small company's migration. Each company is using AWS Config as part of its account management strategy.pWhich combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a landing zone in the security OU of the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone. Provide the account's email address, the account owner's first and last name, and the name of the landing zone created in the security OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In this scenario, the large company already has deployed AWS Control Tower, which means that the landing zone already exists. The Enroll account feature does not require the name of the landing zone. The feature requires the name of the receiving OU.pFor more information about requirements to enroll an AWS account, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/quick-account-provisioning.html"Enroll an Existing Account/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate and apply SCPs in the destination OU to restrict the types of resources that can be created in the small company's account. Assess the impact of the applied SCPs on the small company's account. Delete existing SCPs in the small company's account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If the small company's account has resources deployed in it, SCPs that are applied in the destination OU could cause a failure during enrollment. In addition, the small company has a single account that is not grouped in an organization with all features enabled. Therefore, the account would not contain any SCPs.pFor more information about AWS Control Tower enrollment failure errors, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html"Troubleshootin/a/spana target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/troubleshooting.html"g/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Config conformance pack that contains the policies that are currently applied to the large company's account. Use AWS Config to assess the impact that enrollment in AWS Control Tower will have on the small company's account. Delete the configuration recorder and delivery channels from the AWS Config settings of the small company's account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An AWS Config conformance pack identifies the impact of enrolling an account in AWS Control Tower. This information can be assessed to increase the likelihood of an uneventful enrollment. You must delete the configuration recorder and the AWS Config conformance pack from the small company's account to manage all the AWS Config rules from the organization's management account. There must be no conflicting AWS Config rules on the small company's account.pFor more information about AWS Config conformance packs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/conformance-packs.html"Conformance Packs/a/span.pFor more information about the implementation of AWS Config conformance packs on AWS Control Tower, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/aws-control-tower-detective-guardrails.html"AWS Control Tower Detective Guardrails Conformance Pack/a/span.pFor more information about AWS Control Tower enrollment prerequisites, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/enrollment-prerequisites.html"Prerequisites for Enrollment/a/span.pFor more information about the configuration recorder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/stop-start-recorder.html"Managing the Configuration Recorder/a/span.pFor more information about how to manage AWS Config rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/config-rule-multi-account-deployment.html"Managing AWS Config Rules across All Accounts in Your Organization/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnroll the OU of the small company's account in the large company's AWS Control Tower environment. Specify the destination OU in the large company's AWS Control Tower landing zone as the receiving OU in the request.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The small company has a single AWS account, so the small company will not have an OU to specify. This solution incorrectly combines pieces of two processes: the process to bring an existing account that was registered under AWS Landing Zone into AWS Control Tower, and the process to move a separate account that has not previously joined under AWS Control Tower control. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about AWS Landing Zone migrations to AWS Control Tower, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.comrescriptive-guidance/latest/aws-control-tower/introduction.html"Transitioning from AWS Landing Zone to AWS Control Tower/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWSControlTowerExecution role in the small company's account. Provide the account's email address, the account owner's first and last name, and the destination OU to complete the AWS Control Tower Account Factory enrollment request.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. For AWS Control Tower to successfully enroll an account, the account must have the AWSControlTowerExecution role that grants AdministratorAccess permission. The role also must have an associated trust relationship.pFor more information about AWS Control Tower enrollment prerequisites, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/enrollment-prerequisites.html"Prerequisites for Enrollment/a/span.pFor more information about the AWS Control Tower enrollment process through Account Factory, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/what-is-control-tower.html"What Is AWS Control Tower?/a/span

question_content: pA DevOps team deploys updates to an Amazon API Gateway REST API several times each week by using an AWS CodePipeline pipeline. The REST API automatically reverts to the previous deployment version when the pipeline fails to deploy the REST API. After reverted deployments of the REST API, the DevOps team manually publishes the API Gateway REST API language-specific SDKs to an Amazon S3 bucket for API integrators to use. The API integrators call the REST API from applications that they write.pA DevOps engineer needs to automate the deployment of the language-specific REST API SDKs when the REST API is rolled back.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CodePipeline action immediately after the API Gateway REST API deployment action. Configure the new CodePipeline action to invoke an AWS Lambda function if the previous action fails. Configure the Lambda function to download the REST API SDKs from API Gateway and to upload the SDKs to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodePipeline does not support conditional actions. You can retry a failed action in a particular stage, but you cannot skip a failed action to invoke the next stage. You should use EventBridge to respond to failures and other pipeline-related actions.pFor more information about failed actions in CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-retry.html"Retry a Failed Action in CodePipeline/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new CodePipeline pipeline that runs automatically when the primary pipeline fails to roll back the REST API. Create a manual approval action to complete when the rollback is complete. Create a second action that uses the integration between CodePipeline and API Gateway to export the REST API SDKs to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodePipeline does not support the creation of a new pipeline on failures. If a stage is completed with one or more failed actions, the stage fails and the pipeline execution does not transition to the next stage in the pipeline.pFor more information about failed actions in CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions-retry.html"Retry a Failed Action in CodePipeline/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects the UpdateStage operation on the REST API. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to download the REST API SDKs from API Gateway and to upload the SDKs to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. EventBridge helps to respond to state changes in AWS resources and can invoke a Lambda function. The Lambda function can then call the GetSdk API operation to generate and download an SDK of an API.pFor more information about how to use Lambda with EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-cloudwatchevents.html"Using AWS Lambda with Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events)/a/span.pFor more information about the GetSdk API operation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/api/API_GetSdk.html"GetSdk/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects the CreateDeployment operation on the REST API. Configure the rule to use the integration between EventBridge and API Gateway to export the REST API SDKs from API Gateway to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. When the API reverts to the previous deployment version, a new deployment is not created. An EventBridge rule that detects the CreateDeployment operation on the REST API would not be invoked.pFor more information about how to associate a stage with a different REST API deployment, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-deploy-api-with-console.html"Deploying a REST API from the API Gateway Console/a/span.pFor more information about EventBridge targets for API Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-api-gateway-target.html"Amazon EventBridge Targets for Amazon API Gateway/a/span.

question_content: pA company has an application that monitors user activity on the company's website and mobile apps. The application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis as a write-through cache and uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database for longer storage. When the application receives a request to record a user's action, the application writes to the Redis cluster and the database at the same time. Internal recommendation applications consume the data to produce content recommendations for each user.pDuring peak periods, the recommendation applications cannot generate recommendations for users because of stale and missing data. The Redis cache is configured with cluster mode turned off, and the database is configured with a single read replica.pThe company wants to ensure that the recommendation applications can generate content recommendations during peak periods. A DevOps engineer already has created a new ElastiCache for Redis cluster with cluster mode enabled.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the company's requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a target tracking auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to increase and decrease shards to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's configuration endpoint to access Redis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Auto scaling will provide automatic scaling of shards in the Redis cluster. The data in the cache is partitioned across shards. Therefore, read and write workloads are distributed. The use of the cluster's configuration endpoint ensures that the clients connect to the correct shards, even when the cluster is scaling in or out.pFor more information about ElastiCache for Redis auto scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/AutoScaling.html"Auto Scaling ElastiCache for Redis Clusters/a/span.pFor more information about ElastiCache clusters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Clusters.html"Managing Clusters/a/span.pFor more information about cluster connection endpoints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Endpoints.html"Finding Connection Endpoints/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a target tracking auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to increase and decrease shards to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's read replica endpoint to access Redis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you have cluster mode enabled, the configuration endpoint gives applications the ability to discover primary and read endpoints for each shard in the cluster. The use of the cluster's read replica endpoint would not meet the requirements because there can be more than one read endpoint.pFor more information about cluster connection endpoints, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Endpoints.html"Finding Connection Endpoints/a/span.pFor more information about Redis clusters that have cluster mode enabled, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Replication.Redis.Groups.html#Replication.Redis.Groups.Cluster"Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a/span.pFor more information about how to scale Redis clusters that have cluster mode disabled, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Scaling.RedisReplGrps.html"Scaling Redis (Cluster Mode Disabled) Clusters with Replica Nodes/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a scheduled auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to add read replicas to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the cluster's configuration endpoint to access Redis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Additional read replicas would not distribute the write load across more than one host. Additional read replicas would improve read performance only.pFor more information about how to scale Redis clusters that have cluster mode enabled, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/scaling-redis-cluster-mode-enabled.html"Scaling Clusters in Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a scheduled auto scaling policy for the Redis cluster's ElastiCachePrimaryEngineCPUUtilization metric. Configure the auto scaling policy to add read replicas to the Redis cluster. Update the recommendation applications to use the database's read replica endpoint instead of Redis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Additional read replicas would not distribute the write load across more than one host. Additional read replicas would improve read performance only. Additionally, the use of the database's read replica endpoint would negatively affect performance because the solution would not benefit from a cache layer.pFor more information about Redis clusters that have cluster mode enabled, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/Replication.Redis.Groups.html#Replication.Redis.Groups.Cluster"Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a/span.pFor more information about how to scale Redis clusters that have cluster mode enabled, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/scaling-redis-cluster-mode-enabled.html"Scaling Clusters in Redis (Cluster Mode Enabled)/a/span.

question_content: pA company runs an application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and stores container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company uses AWS CodeDeploy to automatically deploy the application and apply updates.pA DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution that automatically rolls back a deployment if the deployment process fails. The solution also must provide the DevOps engineer with an immediate notification if a deployment fails.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST number of changes to the infrastructure?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Configure Amazon EventBridge to send the DevOps engineer an email message when deployment fails.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. EventBridge cannot send a message to the DevOps engineer.pFor more information about how EventBridge works, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is.html"What Is Amazon EventBridge?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure Amazon CloudWatch metrics for CodeDeploy to create a CloudWatch alarm.
