Configure the CloudWatch alarm to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Subscribe the DevOps engineer to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would create more changes to the infrastructure than the use of an EventBridge event for deployment failures. This solution would require the DevOps engineer to create a CloudWatch alarm and to configure the alarm to use default metrics or customized metrics.pFor more information about CloudWatch alarms, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/AlarmThatSendsEmail.html"Using Amazon CloudWatch Alarms/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that has a detail type of CodeDeploy Instance State-change Notification. Configure the rule to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure the SNS topic as an alarm. Configure rollback to occur when alarm thresholds are met.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy Instance State-change notification is not the correct notification detail type. In addition, you cannot set an SNS topic as an alarm.pFor more information about rollback possibilities with CodeDeploy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-rollback-and-redeploy.html"Redeploy and Roll Back a Deployment with CodeDeploy/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that has a detail type of CodeDeploy Deployment State-change Notification. Configure the rule to send a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure CodeDeploy to roll back when the process fails. Subscribe the DevOps engineer to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A CodeDeploy rollback deployment with an EventBridge rule and an SNS topic meets the requirements and creates the least change to the infrastructure. Additionally, CodeDeploy Deployment State-change Notification is the correct notification detail type.pFor more information about rollback possibilities with CodeDeploy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments-rollback-and-redeploy.html"Redeploy and Roll Back a Deployment with CodeDeploy/a/span.pFor more information about how to monitor deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/monitoring-cloudwatch-events.html"Monitoring Deployments with Amazon CloudWatch Events/a/span.

question_content: pA company has a web application that users access over the internet. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is associated with a security group that allows traffic from the internet. The web application has a local cache on each EC2 instance.pDuring a recent security incident, requests overloaded the web application and caused an outage for the company's customers. In response to the incident, the company added Amazon CloudFront in front of the web application. All customers now access the web application through CloudFront.pA DevOps engineer must implement a solution that routes all requests through CloudFront. The solution also must give the company the ability to block requests based on the content of the requests, such as header or body information.pWhich combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS WAF web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Create rules for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You must create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. AWS WAF rules define how to inspect HTTP and HTTPS web requests and the action to take on a request when the request matches the inspection criteria. AWS WAF can inspect headers and the body of the web request.pFor more information about how to associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a CloudFront distribution, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html"Using AWS WAF to Control Access to Your Content/a/span.pFor more information about AWS WAF rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rules.html"Rules/a/span.pFor more information about how to inspect headers and the body of web requests, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-request-body-inspection.html"Inspection of the Request Body, Headers, and Cookies/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate new ALB listener rules on the existing listeners. Configure the new rules to allow or reject incoming traffic based on whether a custom header matches a value defined by the DevOps engineer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can configure CloudFront and the ALB to prevent internet traffic from directly accessing the ALB. You can configure CloudFront by adding a custom HTTP header to requests that CloudFront sends to the ALB. You can configure the ALB to forward only the requests that contain the custom HTTP header.pFor more information about how to prevent internet traffic from directly accessing an ALB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html"Restricting Access to Application Load Balancers/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for the ALB. Configure the endpoint service to allow requests from CloudFront. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the newly created endpoint service's DNS name.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution does not meet the requirements because only the ALB integrates with PrivateLink. CloudFront does not integrate with PrivateLink.pFor more information about services that integrate with PrivateLink, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latestrivatelink/aws-services-privatelink-support.html"AWS Services That Integrate with AWS PrivateLink/a/span.pFor more information about how to integrate an ALB with PrivateLink, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/application-load-balancer-target.html"Application Load Balancers as Targets/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) for the web application. Update the web application origin in CloudFront to use the OAC. Update the ALB rules to check for the OAC and return an HTTP 403 error if the OAC header is not present.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution does not meet the requirements because CloudFront OAC can be used only with an Amazon S3 bucket origin.pFor more information about CloudFront OAC, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuiderivate-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html"Restricting Access to an Amazon S3 Origin/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Firewall Manager security policy. Attach the security policy to the CloudFront distribution. Use the security policy to attach AWS WAF rule groups for each type of traffic that the company wants to block.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Firewall Manager to roll out AWS WAF rules to CloudFront distributions. However, one of the requirements to use Firewall Manager is that the AWS account must be a member of the AWS Organizations organization where you want to use Firewall Manager policies. This solution and the scenario for this question do not include any indication that the company is using Organizations.pFor more information about how to associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a CloudFront distribution, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html"Using AWS WAF to Control Access to Your Content/a/span.pFor more information about Firewall Manager prerequisites, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-prereq.html"AWS Firewall Manager Prerequisites/a/span.

question_content: pA company manages its AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations. A Development OU is configured for the company's development team to use. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution to provide access to the Development OU for the development team.pThe development team needs programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console for development activities. The development team must not have access to manage IAM permissions. The company has an existing self-managed Active Directory identity provider connection established with AD Connector. Access and security policies must be enforced by an AD group that includes the development team members.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that all features are enabled in Organizations. Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the management account. Select the existing self-managed AD directory with AD Connector as the identity store. Create a permission set that uses the AWS managed PowerUserAccess IAM policy. Assign the permission set to the self-managed development team AD group in IAM Identity Center. Connect the development team AD group to the Development OU accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The integration of the existing identity store (self-managed Active Directory) with IAM Identity Center ensures that security requirements can be enforced through Active Directory. The PowerUserAccess IAM policy allows for development activities to occur and denies access to IAM permissions.pFor more information about IAM Identity Center, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/what-is.html"What is IAM Identity Center?/a/span pFor more information about how to create permission sets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/howtocreatepermissionset.html"Create a Permission Set/a/span.pFor more information about PowerUserAccess and policies for job functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html"AWS Managed Policies for Job Functions/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that all features are enabled in Organizations. Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the delegated administrator account. Select the existing self-managed AD directory with AD Connector as the identity store. Create a permission set that uses the AWS managed AdministratorAccess IAM policy. Assign the permission set to the self-managed development team AD group in IAM Identity Center. Connect the development team AD group to the Development OU accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The use of the AdministratorAccess IAM policy would allow the development team to manage IAM permissions. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about AdministratorAccess and policies for job functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_job-functions.html"AWS Managed Policies for Job Functions/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudFormation StackSets in the management account for deployment to the Development OU. Configure a stack to create a development team IAM group, assign users to the group, and create a custom IAM policy that allows all development activity except management of IAM permissions. Create a script that provides programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console. Synchronize the AD Connector between the self-managed development team AD group and the development team IAM group. Run the script in each Development OU account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With the use of CloudFormation to deploy the same resource to multiple accounts, identities would be synchronized to IAM groups. This solution would require more code and could delay changes that are being pushed to AWS. The DevOps engineer in the scenario should include the existing Active Directory as a single source of truth for identities.pFor more information about CloudFormation StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a/span.pFor more information about AD Connector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html"Active Directory Connector/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudFormation StackSets in the management account for deployment to the Development OU. Configure a stack to create a development team IAM group and users, place the users in the group, assign the AWS managed PowerUserAccess IAM policy to the group, and provide programmatic access and access to the AWS Management Console. Programmatically create new AD Connectors in each target account. Synchronize the development team AD group with the development team IAM group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With the use of CloudFormation to deploy the same resource to multiple accounts, identities would be synchronized to IAM groups. This solution would require more code and could delay changes that are being pushed to AWS. The DevOps engineer in the scenario should include the existing Active Directory as a single source of truth for identities. Additionally, the deployment of multiple AD Connectors would be inefficient for operation and cost.pFor more information about CloudFormation StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html"Working with AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a/span.pFor more information about AD Connector, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html"Active Directory Connector/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses AWS WAF for its web applications. The applications are deployed across multiple AWS Regions. The company's DevOps team has created AWS WAF rule groups that contain commonly used rules. The DevOps team has assigned a security level to each of the company's AWS accounts. The security level represents the sensitivity of the data that each account contains or processes. The AWS accounts are part of an organization in AWS Organizations.pThe DevOps team needs the ability to apply a different set of AWS WAF rule groups to each security level and centrally manage the contents of shared rule groups. Users in the individual AWS accounts must not be able to change the configuration of the shared rule groups.pWhich combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS Config for each combination of Regions and accounts in which AWS WAF will be used.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Config is required for the use of Firewall Manager security policies.pFor more information about Firewall Manager prerequisites, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-prereq.html"AWS Firewall Manager Prerequisites/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTag the AWS accounts with the tags that indicate the desired security policies. In AWS Firewall Manager, create an AWS WAF security policy that targets AWS accounts with those tags. Add the AWS WAF rule groups to the security policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The implementation of Firewall Manager security policies based on tags is possible only on a resource level, not on an account level.pFor more information about Firewall Manager policy scope, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguideolicy-scope.html"AWS Firewall Manager Policy Scope/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an OU for each type of account that needs the shared AWS WAF rule groups. Move each AWS account into the relevant OU.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You must create OUs and associate the accounts with the OUs before you create a Firewall Manager policy for each OU.pFor more information about how Firewall Manager works with Organizations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-fms.html"AWS Firewall Manager and AWS Organizations/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn AWS Firewall Manager, create an AWS WAF security policy that targets accounts in a specified OU. Add the AWS WAF rule groups to the security policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. By creating an OU for each account type, you can use Firewall Manager security policies to deploy a different set of rule groups for each OU.pFor more information about Firewall Manager policy scope, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguideolicy-scope.html"AWS Firewall Manager Policy Scope/a/span.pFor more information about AWS WAF policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html"AWS WAF Policies/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure resource sharing for the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Share the AWS WAF rule groups with all AWS accounts. Associate the AWS WAF rule groups with the existing AWS WAF ACLs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Resource sharing in Organizations is required only for Firewall Manager policies for AWS Network Firewall and Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. In addition, you cannot share an AWS WAF rule group by using AWS RAM.pFor more information about Firewall Manager prerequisites, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-prereq.html"AWS Firewall Manager Prerequisites/a/span.pFor more information about which resources you can share by using AWS RAM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html"Shareable AWS Resources/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS CloudFormation template that contains the AWS WAF rule groups. Deploy the template by using CloudFormation StackSets for the specific OU.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In this solution, individual account users could modify the rule groups by using CloudFormation or by using the AWS CLI, APIs, or console. The requirements state that users must not be able to change the configuration of shared rule groups.pFor more information about CloudFormation stack modification, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks-get-template.html"Modifying a Stack Template/a/span.

question_content: pA company protects its web application by using an AWS WAF web ACL that is associated with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Internal clients and external clients access the web application. The company needs to apply a rate limit on requests to the application. The limit must be higher for requests from internal clients than for requests from external clients.pWhich combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS WAF rule group. Configure rules to match the IP addresses of the internal clients and to apply a label of INTERNAL.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot directly configure AWS WAF rules to match an IP address. To match an IP address, you must create an IP set match rule statement that inspects the request against a set of IP addresses and address ranges.pFor more information about IP set match rule statements, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-ipset-match.html"IP Set Match Rule Statement/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS WAF IP set that contains the IP addresses of the internal clients. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule. Define a separate rate limit for internal clients and external clients. Configure a scope-down statement to apply the internal limit to requests that have the INTERNAL label.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A single AWS WAF rate-based rule tracks the rate of requests for each originating IP address and invokes the rule action on IP addresses that have rates that exceed a limit. With a single AWS WAF rate-based rule, you cannot set up different rate limits for internal clients and external clients.pFor more information about rate-based rule statements, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based.html"Rate-Based Rule Statement/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate two AWS WAF rule groups. In the rule group for internal clients, include a scope-down statement to match requests that have the INTERNAL label. In the rule group for external clients, do not include a scope-down statement. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule in the internal rule group. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value. Create an AWS WAF rate-based rule in the external rule group. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value for requests that do not have the INTERNAL label.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The rule group cannot include a scope-down statement. You can define the scope-down statement only in a rule.pFor more information about rule groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-groups.html"Rule Groups/a/span.pFor more information about scope-down statements, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-scope-down-statements.html"Scope-Down Statements/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS WAF IP set that contains the IP addresses of the internal clients. Create an AWS WAF rule to match requests from the IP set and to apply a label of INTERNAL.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An IP set match rule statement inspects the request against the IP addresses of the internal clients. The AWS WAF rule uses this statement to block or allow web requests based on the IP address of the origin. After the INTERNAL label is defined for the AWS WAF rule, all requests that match the rule are labeled as INTERNAL.pFor more information about IP set match rule statements, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-ipset-match.html"IP Set Match Rule Statement/a/span.pFor more information about labeling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-label-overview.html"How Labeling Works/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS WAF rate-based rule for the internal clients. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value. Configure a scope-down statement to apply to requests that have the INTERNAL label. Create another AWS WAF rate-based rule. Set the rate limit to an appropriate value for requests that do not have the INTERNAL label.

Therefore, you must create two different AWS WAF rate-based rules and set the rate limit of the two rules in accordance with the requirements. question_content: pA company has a VPC that consists of a public subnet and a private subnet. The company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in the private subnet. An Application Load Balancer is in the public subnet and distributes traffic to the EC2 instances.pThe company has enabled Amazon GuardDuty for the account. The company's DevOps team has a list of external IP ranges that is updated each day. The list is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the account. A DevOps engineer needs to configure GuardDuty to create a GuardDuty finding when traffic to the application originates from an IP range in the external IP range list.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the publicIp filter attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A finding filter refines findings against criteria that you specify. The publicIp attribute would apply to a resource's public IP address if a public IP address exists. A finding filter would not cause GuardDuty to generate the initial finding from the external IP range.pFor more information about finding filters and filter attributes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_filter-findings.html"Filtering Findings/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a threat list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the threat list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A threat list is the correct component in GuardDuty to monitor for a connection that originates from a list of IP ranges. EventBridge can invoke the Lambda function on a schedule to refresh the list in GuardDuty.pFor more information about threat lists, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_upload-lists.html"Working with Trusted IP Lists and Threat Lists/a/span.pFor more information about how to update threat lists, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_upload-lists.html#update-lists-procedure"To Update Trusted IP Lists and Threat Lists/a/span.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to schedule Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html"Tutorial: Schedule AWS Lambda Functions Using EventBridge/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure a trusted IP list in GuardDuty. Set the source as the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to refresh the trusted IP list in GuardDuty to match the list of external IP ranges in the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you match a list of IP addresses against a trusted IP list, you will not generate any findings. A threat list is more appropriate.pFor more information about the two types of lists in GuardDuty, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_upload-lists.html"Working with Trusted IP Lists and Threat Lists/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs daily and invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve the most recent list of external IP ranges from the S3 bucket. For each IP range in the list, configure the Lambda function to create a GuardDuty finding filter on the localIp filter attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A finding filter refines findings against criteria that you specify. The localIp attribute would apply to a resource's local IPv4 address. A finding filter would not cause GuardDuty to generate the initial finding from the external IP range.pFor more information about finding filters and filter attributes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_filter-findings.html"Filtering Findings/a/span.

question_content: pA company needs to scan code changes for security issues before deployment and must prevent noncompliant code from being deployed. The company uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that starts when code changes occur. The code changes occur many times each day.pThe company's security team supports a third-party application for code scans and has provided command-line integration steps to submit code scans. The code scan step requires a user name and password.pWhich solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new AWS CodeBuild project. Configure the user name and password in an environment variable. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The company can create its own environment variable in CodeBuild projects. However, the use of environment variables to store sensitive values is not recommended.pFor more information about environment variables in CodeBuild, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-env-vars.html"Environment Variables in Build Environments/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Read the secret from Secrets Manager. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Secrets Manager can store secrets, including passwords, securely. You can retrieve secrets programmatically by invoking the Secrets Manager API. In addition, CodeBuild integrates with Secrets Manager.pFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What Is AWS Secrets Manager?/a/spanpFor more information about how to use CodeBuild with Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/integrating-codebuild.html"How AWS CodeBuild Uses AWS Secrets Manager/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new AWS CodeBuild project. Store the user name and password as a string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Read the string from Parameter Store. Use the user name and password to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store can store secrets securely with a SecureString parameter. However, this solution stores the user name and password as a string. The storage of sensitive data in a String parameter or StringList parameter is not recommended.pFor more information about Parameter Store, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html"AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpload the user name and password in an encrypted JSON file to an Amazon S3 bucket that has a specific policy to allow only administrators to read the file. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Use the user name and password from the file in Amazon S3 to run the command-line integration steps. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to include a new scan stage. In the new scan stage, include a test action that uses the newly created CodeBuild project.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Bucket policies and user policies can restrict access to S3 buckets. However, this solution is not the most secure option. Amazon S3 was not designed to store passwords.pFor more information about S3 bucket policies and user policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-iam-policies.html"Bucket Policies and User Policies/a/span.pFor more information about Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html"What Is Amazon S3?/a/span

question_content: pA company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The company's DevOps team analyzes the CPU and memory metrics of the company's Amazon EC2 instances and applies an Underutilized tag to some resources in the member accounts. The DevOps team needs to prevent users in the member accounts from modifying or deleting these tags.pWhat is the MOST operationally efficient way to meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the member accounts, deploy an AWS Lambda function by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Configure the Lambda function to run the DescribeTags API operation and to update the tag values if there is a mismatch. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every time a CreateTags or DeleteTags API event occurs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution could solve the problem, but it is not the most operationally efficient solution because it requires the development and management of a custom Lambda function. Because the account uses Organizations, you could use SCPs instead.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to run a Lambda function, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-cloudwatchevents.html"Using AWS Lambda with Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn the member accounts, deploy an AWS Lambda function by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Configure the Lambda function to run the DescribeTags API operation and to update the tag values if there is a mismatch. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function every 30 minutes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution could solve the problem, but it is not the most operationally efficient solution because it requires the development and management of a custom Lambda function. Because the account uses Organizations, you could use SCPs instead. Additionally, the invocation of the Lambda function every 30 minutes would be less cost-effective.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to run a Lambda function, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-cloudwatchevents.html"Using AWS Lambda with Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events)/a/span.pFor more information about how to create scheduled rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html"Creating an Amazon EventBridge Rule That Runs on a Schedule/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an SCP that denies the CreateTags API action and the DeleteTags API action for the Underutilized tag to authorized principals. Attach the SCP to the OU in the management account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. By using SCPs, you can prevent users in the member accounts from modifying or deleting the tags. You can create an SCP that explicitly denies the CreateTags action and the DeleteTags action except by authorized principals. This solution is the most operationally efficient way to restrict tag access and is more cost-effective than using a Lambda function.pFor more information about how to prevent changes to tags, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_examples_tagging.html#example-require-restrict-tag-mods-to-admin"Prevent Tags from Being Modified Except by Authorized Principals/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a tag policy that denies the CreateTags API action and the DeleteTags API action for the Underutilized tag to authorized principals. Attach the tag policy to the OU in the management account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Tag policies can help standardize tags across resources in an organization. With tag policies, you can specify the case convention and tag values that the resource can receive in the key or value. However, tag policies cannot prevent some principals from deleting or updating tags.pFor more information about tag policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html"Tag Policies/a/span.pFor more information about tag policy syntax, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_example-tag-policies.html"Tag Policy Syntax and Examples/a/span.

question_content: pA company has deployed a new Amazon API Gateway API that retrieves the cost of items for the company's online store. An AWS Lambda function supports the API and retrieves the data from an Amazon DynamoDB table. The API's latency increases during times of peak usage each day. However, the latency of the DynamoDB table reads is constant throughout the day.pA DevOps engineer configures DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the DynamoDB table, and the API latency decreases throughout the day. The DevOps engineer then configures Lambda provisioned concurrency with a limit of two concurrent invocations. This change reduces the latency during normal usage. However, the company is still experiencing higher latency during times of peak usage than during times of normal usage.pWhich set of additional steps should the DevOps engineer take to produce the LARGEST decrease in API latency?

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the read capacity of the DynamoDB table. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to manage provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The DevOps engineer in the scenario already improved the latency of the DynamoDB table by using DAX. An increase in the read capacity of the table would not provide any additional improvement and would not be efficient.pFor more information about DynamoDB read/write capacity mode, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadWriteCapacityMode.html"Read/Write Capacity Mode/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable caching in API Gateway. Stop using provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. API Gateway caching would be beneficial. However, a lack of provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function would have an adverse impact because the provisioned concurrency previously improved the latency during normal usage.pFor more information about provisioned concurrency for Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dgrovisioned-concurrency.html"Configuring Provisioned Concurrency/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDelete the DAX cluster for the DynamoDB table. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to manage provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In the scenario, DAX already provided decreased latency. A deletion of the DAX cluster likely would increase the latency from this tier.pFor more information about DAX, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html#DAX.use-cases"Use Cases for DAX/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable caching in API Gateway. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to manage provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Because the API in the scenario is a pricing API, calls and returned results likely will be similar or identical. API Gateway caching will provide lower response times to identical calls and will improve the performance. Additionally, the DevOps engineer previously configured Lambda provisioned concurrency that decreased latency. The use of AWS Application Auto Scaling will improve the performance under heavier loads.pFor more information about API Gateway caching, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html"Enabling API Caching to Enhance Responsiveness/a/span.pFor more information about provisioned concurrency for Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dgrovisioned-concurrency.html"Configuring Provisioned Concurrency/a/span.

question_content: pA software-as-a-service (SaaS) company is using AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy its primary .NET application. The autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH event occurs when a new EC2 instance is successfully launched, not when EC2 instances are terminated.pFor more information about the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH event, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html"Get Amazon SNS Notifications When Your Auto Scaling Group Scales/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Add an AWS Lambda function trigger to the SQS queue. Apply a notification configuration for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH notification type to all the existing Auto Scaling groups.

You also do not need to create a Lambda function to send notifications for this scenario. Additionally, the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH event occurs when a new EC2 instance is successfully launched, not when EC2 instances are terminated.pFor more information about Amazon SQS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html"What Is Amazon Simple Queue Service?/a/spanpFor more information about the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH event, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-sns-notifications.html"Get Amazon SNS Notifications When Your Auto Scaling Group Scales/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the email addresses of all operations team members to the SNS topic. You also do not need to create a Lambda function to send notifications for this scenario.pFor more information about Amazon SQS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/welcome.html"What Is Amazon Simple Queue Service?/a/span

question_content: pA company uses AWS Organizations to manage 400 AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer is deploying a new feature to all member accounts in all AWS Regions by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. The deployment is taking a long time.pWhich combination of actions will lead to the LOWEST deployment time for future deployments? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the Retain Stacks option to True.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. When the Retain Stacks option is set to True, you can keep stacks and their resources running even after you remove stacks from a stack set. When you retain stacks, CloudFormation keeps stacks in individual accounts and Regions intact. The Retain Stacks option does not have an impact on deployment time.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the Region concurrency to Parallel.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Parallel concurrency deploys StackSets operations into all specified Regions in parallel. Parallel concurrency is not the default configuration. Without this action, the deployment would happen one Region at a time and would require more time overall.pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html#stacksets-concepts-opsSection"StackSets Concepts/a/span. pFor more information about parallel Region concurrency, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html#stackset-ops-options"Stack Set Operation Options/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the Region concurrency to Sequential.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Sequential concurrency deploys StackSets operations into one Region at a time as specified by Region deployment order. Sequential deployment is the default configuration and would slow down deployment because deployment would occur only one Region at a time.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the maximum concurrent accounts number to 25.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The maximum concurrent accounts option specifies the maximum number or percentage of target accounts in which an operation performs at one time. If you set the maximum concurrent accounts number to 25 for this scenario, you would deploy to 25 accounts at a time. This action would not result in the lowest deployment time.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the maximum concurrent accounts percentage to 25.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The maximum concurrent accounts option specifies the maximum number or percentage of target accounts in which an operation performs at one time. If you set the maximum concurrent accounts percentage to 25 for this scenario, you would deploy to 100 accounts at a time. Therefore, this action provides the lowest deployment time.pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html#stacksets-concepts-opsSection"StackSets Concepts/a/span. pFor more information about the maximum concurrent accounts option, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html#stackset-ops-options"Stack Set Operation Options/a/span.

question_content: pA company has an online application that performs compute-intensive processing of large images. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Each EC2 instance operates at 100% CPU when the instance processes images.pWhen the application receives an image, the application stores the image in an Amazon S3 bucket and generates an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message that includes the image's location. An EC2 instance retrieves the SQS message from the SQS queue and processes the image that is referenced in the message. If the message fails processing, the message goes to a dead-letter queue. The  EC2 instance does not report any custom metrics to Amazon CloudWatch.pDuring a typical day, the application processes hundreds to thousands of images each hour. The company needs to scale the application's ability to process images based on the amount of processing work that must be performed. A DevOps engineer is implementing a CloudWatch alarm to scale the Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances.pWhich CloudWatch metric should the DevOps engineer use for the alarm to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe average memory utilization of the EC2 instances
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Memory utilization metrics are not available by default. You would need to configure the instances to send this metric from the operating system through scripts, code, or the CloudWatch agent.pFor more information about how to use the CloudWatch agent to deliver additional metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/metrics-collected-by-CloudWatch-agent.html"Metrics Collected by the CloudWatch Agent/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe average CPU utilization of the EC2 instances
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In the scenario, each EC2 instance's CPU utilization is 100% during processing. Therefore, average CPU utilization is not a good way to determine how much processing work the application needs to perform.pFor more information about CPU utilization of an EC2 instance, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html#ec2-cloudwatch-metrics"Instance Metrics/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe approximate count of messages in the dead-letter queue
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The dead-letter queue is for messages that could not be processed. Therefore, the approximate count of messages in the dead-letter queue is not a good indicator of how much processing work the application needs to perform.pFor more information about dead-letter queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html"Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queues/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe approximate count of messages in the SQS queue
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The approximate count of messages in the SQS queue is an indicator of the amount of work that the application needs to perform. A change in the number of EC2 instances to match the amount of work provides the best use of resources.pFor more information about available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html"Available CloudWatch Metrics for Amazon SQS/a/span.pFor more information about scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html"Scaling Based on Amazon SQS/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses AWS Organizations. The company needs to provide a set of packaged libraries for member accounts to use. The company's tooling team has an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that consists of the source AWS CodeCommit repository and an AWS CodeBuild project that packages the libraries. However, the creation of a domain and a repository for each package and the configuration of domain policies for the member accounts would require additional operational overhead.pFor more information about domains, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/domains.html"Working with Domains in CodeArtifact/a/span.pFor more information about domain policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/domain-policies.html"Domain Policies/a/span.

answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeArtifact supports resource-based permissions to control access to the domains and repositories. However, the creation of a domain and a repository for each package and the configuration of repository policies for the member accounts would require additional operational overhead.pFor more information about repositories, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/repos.html"Working with Repositories in CodeArtifact/a/span.pFor more information about repository policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/repo-policies.html"Repository Policies/a/span.

question_content: pA company stores purchase history in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company needs other workloads that run on AWS to react to data changes in the table.pThe company has enabled a DynamoDB stream on the table. Three existing AWS Lambda functions have an event source mapping configured for the DynamoDB stream. The company's application developers plan to add other applications that will need to react to changes in the table. A DevOps engineer must design an architecture that will give the additional consumers this functionality.pWhich solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the event bus. Update the original Lambda functions to react to events in the event bus. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the event bus as an event source.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution addresses the fact that more than two table stream readers can introduce read throttling. By having a single function read from the table stream and moving those events to an EventBridge event bus, you shift the design from a pull-based (polling) design to a push-based (notification) design. Therefore, this solution increases the scalability of many event-reacting workloads. This solution is also operationally efficient because it is event driven and does not require additional components to build, deploy, or manage.pFor more information about how DynamoDB streams work, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html"Change Data Capture for DynamoDB Streams/a/span.pFor more information about DynamoDB Streams quotas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html#limits-dynamodb-streams"DynamoDB Streams/a/span.pFor more information about how to create EventBridge rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule.html"Creating Amazon EventBridge Rules that React to Events/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the SQS queue. Update the original Lambda functions to react to entries in the SQS queue. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the SQS queue as an event source.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. With this solution, multiple functions would read from a single SQS queue for different workloads. A competing consumer failure mode would result, and not all functions would receive the table data change event. Only one consumer would receive each change event. You could implement a fanout pattern to multiple SQS queues for individual functions to process individual workloads. However, such a solution typically uses an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with filtered subscriptions for each queue for functions to process.pFor more information about how to scale by using Amazon SQS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-throughput-horizontal-scaling-and-batching.html"Increasing Throughput Using Horizontal Scaling and Action Batching/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create a new Lambda function that uses the existing DynamoDB stream as an event source. Configure the new Lambda function to post those events to the Kinesis data stream. Update the original Lambda functions to subscribe to records in the Kinesis data stream. As other applications need the events, configure the applications to use the Kinesis data stream as an event source.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is not as operationally efficient as the correct answer because this solution is not as scalable. The addition of new applications and functions will create additional management overhead that is related to the Kinesis data stream.pFor more information about Kinesis Data Streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html"What Is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity mode. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions to use provisioned concurrency.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DynamoDB streams operate asynchronously. There is no performance impact on a table if a stream is enabled. On-demand capacity will not address read throttles on the table stream or improve performance. An increase in memory and the use of provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions also will not address table stream read-based throttling. Provisioned concurrency decreases function cold starts and increases memory that is available to the functions. Provisioned concurrency improves only function performance.pFor more information about how DynamoDB streams work, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html"Change Data Capture for DynamoDB Streams/a/span.pFor more information about provisioned concurrency for Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dgrovisioned-concurrency.html"Configuring Provisioned Concurrency/a/span.

question_content: pA company has resources in an AWS account. The resources are deployed to multiple AWS Regions. In the AWS account, the company also has IAM users that access the AWS Management Console. The company has configured an AWS CloudTrail multi-Region trail to log management events for read and write activity to an Amazon S3 bucket.pA DevOps engineer must implement a solution that tracks all AWS Management Console login failures. When a console login failure occurs, the company's security team must receive an email notification in near real time.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Athena table from the CloudTrail logs in the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the AWS SDK to query the Athena table. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 60 minutes. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic when a failed login is detected in the CloudTrail logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would work but is not as operationally efficient as the correct answer. This solution is less operationally efficient because it requires the creation of a Lambda function to detect failed login events by running queries on the Athena table. This solution also would take time to fetch the events of the last 60 minutes in every invocation.pFor more information about how to run Athena queries, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/querying-athena-tables.html"Running SQL Queries Using Amazon Athena/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function to process CloudTrail logs from the S3 bucket. Use S3 event notifications to invoke the Lambda function when a new object is created in the S3 bucket. Write Lambda function code to parse the logs from Amazon S3 and match console login failure events. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would work but is not as operationally efficient as the correct answer. This solution is less operationally efficient because it requires the creation of a Lambda function to analyze logs.pFor more information about how to enable CloudTrail logging for Amazon S3,  see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/enable-cloudtrail-logging-for-s3.html"Enabling CloudTrail Event Logging for S3 Buckets and Objects/a/span.pFor examples of CloudTrail log file entries, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-understanding-s3-entries.html"CloudTrail Log File Entries for Amazon S3 and S3 on Outposts/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. In the us-east-1 Region, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses AWS events as the event source. Use a filter for console login failure events. Configure the SNS topic as the rule's target.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. IAM user login events are registered only in us-east-1 within the CloudTrail event history. This solution does not require any additional configuration change to CloudTrail. An EventBridge rule can detect CloudTrail login failure events and send notifications to an email address that is subscribed to an SNS topic.pFor more information about CloudTrail IAM events, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-concepts.html#cloudtrail-concepts-global-service-events"Global Service Events/a/span.pFor more information about EventBridge target options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html"Amazon EventBridge Targets/a/span.pFor more information about how to send email through Amazon SNS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-email-notifications.html"Email Notifications/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses AWS events as the event source. Create an AWS Lambda function. Write Lambda function code to match console login failure events from inbound data from EventBridge. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team's email address to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would work but is not as operationally efficient as the correct answer. This solution is less operationally efficient because it requires the creation of EventBridge rules in all Regions and requires the creation of a Lambda function. You could replace the Lambda function with EventBridge event patterns.pFor more information about the creation of event patterns, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-event-patterns.html"Amazon EventBridge Event Patterns/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses a fleet of on-premises servers for CPU-intensive workloads. The servers run a Docker image that retrieves messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. Messages that the servers fail to process are put into an SQS dead-letter queue.pThe company recently had a power outage that caused messages to go unprocessed at the on-premises data center. The company wants to add additional queue processing capacity. A DevOps engineer needs to build a resilient system that can process workloads by using the on-premises servers. The system also must have the ability to process workloads in the cloud when some or all of the on-premises servers are offline or when additional workload capacity is needed.pThe DevOps engineer uses the Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) agent to join the on-premises servers to an Amazon ECS Anywhere cluster. The DevOps engineer pushes the Docker image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and creates an ECS task that uses the image.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate capacity provider and an ECS task from the same ECR image. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS dead-letter queue to automatically scale the new ECS cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution sends messages that are not processed to the dead-letter queue. However, the dead-letter queue does not have a metric to monitor the approximate number of messages visible in the queue. Therefore, you cannot create an alarm on this metric to automatically scale the new ECS cluster.pFor more information about SQS dead-letter queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html"Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queues/a/span.pFor more information about available SQS metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html"Available CloudWatch Metrics for Amazon SQS/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pReplace the ECS Anywhere cluster with an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate capacity provider. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue to automatically scale the new ECS cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The replacement of the ECS Anywhere cluster with an ECS cluster that uses the Fargate capacity provider does not provide the ability to register an external instance to the cluster. With this configuration, the CloudWatch alarm that is based on the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue cannot use the fleet of on-premises servers to launch tasks.pFor more information about ECS Anywhere, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-anywhere.html"External Instances (Amazon ECS Anywhere)/a/span.pFor more information about available SQS metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html"Available CloudWatch Metrics for Amazon SQS/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate capacity provider and an ECS task from the same ECR image. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue to automatically scale the tasks that are deployed in the new ECS cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution meets all the requirements. Both ECS clusters are pulling workloads from the same SQS queue. The SQS queue size can be used to determine the number of Fargate tasks that need to be configured on the ECS cluster. If any ECS Anywhere-based servers fail, the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue will change and can cause a scaling action. This design successfully decouples the on-premises containers and cloud containers to provide resiliency and workload-based scaling.pFor more information about how to scale ECS workloads, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html"Service Auto Scaling/a/span.pFor more information about ECS Anywhere, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-anywhere.html"External Instances (Amazon ECS Anywhere)/a/span.pFor more information about Amazon ECS on Fargate, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html"Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate capacity provider and an ECS task from the same ECR image. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue to automatically scale the ECS Anywhere cluster.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The approximate number of messages visible in the SQS queue is the correct metric to scale the cluster. However, because the alarm automatically scales only the ECS Anywhere cluster, this solution does not meet the resiliency requirements.pFor more information about ECS launch types, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/launch_types.html"Amazon ECS Launch Types/a/span.pFor more information about ECS Anywhere, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-anywhere.html"External Instances (Amazon ECS Anywhere)/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer wants to deploy a new AWS Lambda function to all accounts in the organization by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets. The DevOps engineer uses a delegated administrator account to deploy the stack sets to the member accounts. The stack operation keeps failing, and the stack instance status is OUTDATED.pWhich actions should the DevOps engineer take to remediate this error? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the AWS Region is the same for the stack sets and the target resources.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudFormation StackSets can deploy resources to any Region and does not require the stack sets to be in the same Region as the target resources.pFor more information about StackSets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html"StackSets Concepts/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the delegated administrator account has a trust relationship with the target account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Every account that you deploy a stack instance to requires a role that has a trust relationship with the administrator account. Otherwise, the deployment will fail.pFor more information about how to troubleshoot StackSets issues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-troubleshooting.html"Troubleshooting AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the resources in the stacks do not have termination protection enabled by default.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Termination protection would not cause any issues during deployment of a stack set. Instead, termination protection could cause an issue during attempts to delete a stack.pFor more information about termination protection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-protect-stacks.html"Protecting a Stack from Being Deleted/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the CloudFormation template is creating unique global resources.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Some resources, such as Amazon S3 buckets and IAM roles, are globally unique. An attempt to create these resources in the same account but different Regions can cause a StackSets deployment to fail.pFor more information about how to troubleshoot StackSets issues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-troubleshooting.html"Troubleshooting AWS CloudFormation StackSets/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy the stack sets from the management account and not from the delegated administrator account.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Similar to the management account, delegated administrator accounts have full permissions to deploy resources to accounts in an organization. If the delegated administrator account has a trust relationship with the target account, the delegated administrator account would be able to deploy the stack sets.pFor more information about delegated administrator accounts, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-delegated-admin.html"Register a Delegated Administrator/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'{/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'    "Version": "2012-10-17",/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'    "Statement": [/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'        {/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            "Sid": "OnlySpecificRegions",/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            "Effect": "Deny",/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            "Action": [/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                "*"/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            ],/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            "Resource": "*",/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            "Condition": {/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                "StringNotEquals": {/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                    "aws:RequestedRegion": [/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                        "us-east-2",/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                        "us-west-2"/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                    ]/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'                }/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'            }/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'        }/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'    ]/spanpspan style='font-family: "Courier New";'}/span

question_content: pA company hosts a multi-tenant application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run Windows Server and are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses a license file on the instances that can be updated on the instances without customer disruption. When a new customer purchases access to the application, the company's licensing team adds a new license key to a file in an Amazon S3 bucket. After the license file is updated, the operations team manually updates the EC2 instances.pA DevOps engineer needs to automate the EC2 instance file update process. The automated process must decrease the time for EC2 instances to get the updated license file and must notify the operations team about success or failure of the update process.pThe DevOps engineer creates a resource group in AWS Resource Groups. The resource group uses a tag that the Auto Scaling group applies to the EC2 instances.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the license file is updated in the S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunRemoteScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notifications for event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED to send email notifications to the operations team.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon SES does not integrate with Systems Manager to send notifications about the status of commands from Run Command.pFor more information about the integration of Amazon SNS with Systems Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-notifications.html"Monitoring Systems Manager Status Changes Using Amazon SNS Notifications/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the license file is updated in the S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunPowerShellScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED. Subscribe the email addresses of the operations team members to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution is the most cost-effective option because the Lambda function runs only when the license file is updated. S3 event notifications can invoke the Lambda function, and the AWS-RunPowerShellScript document runs operations in a Windows operating system. In addition, 50% concurrency decreases the deployment time. Amazon SNS provides the appropriate notification messages.pFor more information about S3 event notifications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html"Event Notification Types and Destinations/a/span.pFor more information about Windows PowerShell commands, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/walkthrough-powershell.html"Walkthrough: Use the AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell with Run Command/a/span.pFor more information about how to send commands to an EC2 fleet, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/send-commands-multiple.html"Run Commands at Scale/a/span.pFor more information about the integration of Amazon SNS with Systems Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-notifications.html"Monitoring Systems Manager Status Changes Using Amazon SNS Notifications/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that runs each hour to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the AWS-RunPowerShellScript document to download the updated license file. Specify the command from Lambda to run on the application's resource group with 50% concurrency. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED. Subscribe the email addresses of the operations team members to the SNS topic.

Therefore, this solution is not the most cost-effective option.pFor more information about invocation costs for Lambda, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/lambdaricing/"AWS Lambda Pricing/a/span.pFor more information about Windows PowerShell commands, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/walkthrough-powershell.html"Walkthrough: Use the AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell with Run Command/a/span.pFor more information about how to send commands to an EC2 fleet, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/send-commands-multiple.html"Run Commands at Scale/a/span.

Configure Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notifications for event notifications of SUCCESS and FAILED to send email notifications to the operations team.
