However, the scheduled invocations would invoke the Lambda function every hour and would generate charges even if there is no change in the license file. Therefore, this solution is not the most cost-effective option. In addition, Amazon SES does not integrate with Systems Manager to send notifications about the status of commands from Run Command.pFor more information about invocation costs for Lambda, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/lambdaricing/"AWS Lambda Pricing/a/span.pFor more information about the integration of Amazon SNS with Systems Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-notifications.html"Monitoring Systems Manager Status Changes Using Amazon SNS Notifications/a/span.

question_content: pA company needs to identify AWS Lambda functions that are running end-of-life (EOL) language runtimes in an AWS account. The account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations and has only the AWS Basic Support plan. A DevOps engineer must create a monitoring solution that notifies the company about any Lambda functions that are running EOL runtimes.pThe company already has created an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The company also has configured AWS Config for the account.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do to meet the requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Config custom rule that is associated with a Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to query the AWS Health API for EOL runtime events and to publish notifications to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot access the AWS Health API by using the AWS Basic Support plan.pFor more information about the AWS Health API and its supported AWS Support plans, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/health-api.html"Accessing the AWS Health API/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that has an AWS Health event pattern. Configure the rule to filter for specific health events for EOL runtimes and to publish notifications to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use EventBridge to detect and react to AWS Health events. Based on rules that you create, EventBridge invokes one or more target actions when an event matches the values that you specify. Depending on the type of event, you can capture event information, initiate additional events, send notifications, and take corrective action.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to detect and react to AWS Health events, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/cloudwatch-events-health.html"Monitoring AWS Health Events with Amazon EventBridge/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK managed rule in AWS Config. Configure the rule to report resources that have EOL runtimes as NON_COMPLIANT and to publish notifications to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is not the most operationally efficient approach because the LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK managed rule in AWS Config requires you to provide a list of EOL runtimes. As time passes, you would need to update the list to include new runtimes.pFor more information about the LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK managed rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/lambda-function-settings-check.html"lambda-function-settings-check/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS Trusted Advisor for the AWS account. Update the Trusted Advisor preferences to publish notifications to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Trusted Advisor can detect EOL runtimes. However, this functionality is not available with the AWS Basic Support plan. In addition, Trusted Advisor cannot send notifications to an SNS topic.pFor more information about AWS Support plans for Trusted Advisor, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html"AWS Trusted Advisor/a/span.pFor more information about Trusted Advisor notification options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/get-started-with-aws-trusted-advisor.html#preferences-trusted-advisor-console"Preferences/a/span.

question_content: pA company is using an Amazon API Gateway API and an AWS Lambda function to host a microservice. The microservice accesses pricing data in an Amazon DynamoDB table for the company's online store.pInterest in the online store has increased. As a result, latency issues and throttling on the DynamoDB table are occurring when a specific query runs. Some internal services access the DynamoDB table directly. No caching is enabled for the current solution.pA DevOps engineer notices that repeat requests to the API are taking the same amount of time as unique requests. The DevOps engineer must reduce the latency for the repeat requests to the API and must reduce the throttling on the DynamoDB table.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable caching for API Gateway stages. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution provides caching for API Gateway and the DynamoDB table. Both caching methods are necessary because of the internal calls from the Lambda function. The API Gateway caching reduces the number of repeated calls to the endpoint and improves the latency of requests to the API. DAX provides fast response for access to eventually consistent data.pFor more information about API Gateway caching, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html"Enabling API Caching to Enhance Responsiveness/a/span.pFor more information about DAX, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html"In-Memory Acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable caching for API Gateway stages. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached caching for the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Memcached provides an in-memory caching solution that you can use to retrieve data with low latency and high throughput. However, Memcached is not available for DynamoDB.pFor more information about ElastiCache for Memcached, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/mem-ug/WhatIs.html"What Is Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The use of provisioned concurrency could improve the Lambda function's performance but would not reduce repeat requests to the API. The use of DAX would reduce the throttling on the DynamoDB table.pFor more information about Lambda concurrency, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html"Configuring Reserved Concurrency/a/span.pFor more information about DAX, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html"In-Memory Acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Increase the RCUs for the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution could improve the performance of the Lambda function and the DynamoDB table. However, this solution would not reduce repeat requests to the API.pFor more information about Lambda concurrency, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html"Configuring Reserved Concurrency/a/span.pFor more information about DynamoDB read/write capacity mode, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadWriteCapacityMode.html"Read/Write Capacity Mode/a/span.

question_content: pA company runs its software products as microservices on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters that are powered by Amazon EC2 instances. The instances are launched from publicly available Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMIs that AWS maintains and updates.pDuring a compliance review, a DevOps team receives an urgent request to install a custom security package on the Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMIs before the AMIs are launched in Amazon ECS. The team must implement a solution that does not affect the ECS task launch time. The solution must validate the security package before a new image can be used. The team also needs access to image build logs that capture specific error messages in real time.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon S3 bucket to store the custom security package. Use EC2 user data to add a script to pull the package from Amazon S3 and install the package. Add validation scripts in the user data to run test cases. For logging, pre-install the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the user data operations in real time. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use EC2 user data to perform configuration tasks and run scripts after the instance starts. However, this solution slows down the instance bootstrap. At startup time, the instance must download and install the package before the instance can be ready to start the test. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements of least operational effort.pFor more information about commands and user data, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/user-data.html"Run Commands on Your Linux Instance at Launch/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse EC2 Image Builder to configure a new image pipeline. Import the current Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMI as the base image. Create a new image recipe that uses the imported base image. Configure custom security package installation. Configure an EC2 Image Builder component to validate and test the built images. Access EC2 Image Builder logs through Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use EC2 Image Builder to configure an image pipeline. However, if you import the Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMI as the base image, the image will become outdated when AWS releases new optimized images. When a new Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 AMI become available, you should update the pipeline.pFor more information about EC2 Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/how-image-builder-works.html"How EC2 Image Builder Works/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse EC2 Image Builder to configure a new image pipeline. Create a new image recipe that uses AWS managed Amazon ECS-optimized Amazon Linux 2 as the base image. Configure custom security package installation. Configure an EC2 Image Builder component to validate and test the built images. Access EC2 Image Builder logs through Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. By using EC2 Image Builder with an image recipe, you can define the latest base image to use as the starting point to create a new image. With auto-versioning feature options, EC2 Image Builder uses the latest available operating system version. The image recipe defines the set of components that you can add to customize the image and to verify that everything is working as expected. At the last stage, EC2 Image Builder produces an AMI that you can use for the launch EC2 instance. This new AMI already has the security packages in place, and no bootstrapping is required. EC2 Image Builder streams logs to CloudWatch, which can help examine and troubleshoot issues by creating metric filters to capture any error message.pFor more information about EC2 Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/how-image-builder-works.html"How EC2 Image Builder Works/a/span.pFor more information about how to create an image pipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/start-build-image-pipeline.html"Create an Image Pipeline Using the EC2 Image Builder Console Wizard/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Systems Manager. Ensure that Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is pre-installed on the cluster EC2 instances. Create a Systems Manager Automation custom runbook that can run a script to install the custom security package and run test cases. Create a new EC2 tag key and value. Ensure that all new EC2 instances launch with the tag. Configure Systems Manager Automation to run the custom runbook on all instances that have the EC2 tag. For logging, pre-install the Amazon CloudWatch agent to stream the user data operations in real time. Use CloudWatch filters to capture specific error messages.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Systems Manager Automation to create a custom runbook that runs a script to install the custom security package and run test cases. However, this solution slows down the bootstrap of the instance. At startup time, the instance must download and install the package before the instance can be ready to start the test. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirements of least operational effort.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation runbooks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-documents.html"Creating Your Own Runbooks/a/span.

question_content: pA company has many AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has a CI/CD pipeline that builds Docker images and publishes the images to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The ECR repository is encrypted by an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The KMS key grants permission to an IAM role that the CI/CD pipeline uses.pThe company needs to make the Docker images available to all accounts in the organization and must maintain the current level of security for the images.pWhich combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the KMS key to allow all accounts in the organization to use the key.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. To provide access to all the associated AWS accounts in the organization, the KMS key needs a statement that allows KMS operations with a condition that is based on the organization ID. You can achieve this functionality by adding the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key to the principal element in a resource-based policy with AWS KMS.pFor more information about the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_condition-keys.html#condition-keys-principalorgid"aws:PrincipalOrgID/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new KMS key that allows all accounts in the organization to use the key.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot change the KMS key that is used in an ECR repository without replacing the repository.pFor more information about KMS update requirements in Amazon ECR, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-ecr-repository-encryptionconfiguration.html"AWS::ECR::Repository EncryptionConfiguration/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ECR repository policy to allow all accounts in the organization to pull the images.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon ECR uses resource-based permissions to manage access to repositories. You can specify which IAM user or role will have access to a repository. In the scenario for this question, an ECR repository policy with a condition that specifies the organization ID grants least privilege access to the repository.pFor more information about ECR repository policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html"Private Repository Policies/a/span.pFor more information about organization ID identifiers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_condition-keys.html#condition-keys-principalorgid"aws:PrincipalOrgID/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a cross-account IAM role that all accounts in the organization can assume. Give the newly created role permissions to pull the images.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The role will not have the KMS permissions that are required to interact with an encrypted repository. In addition, you are not following best practices if you make a role assumable by all accounts in an organization.pFor more information about IAM policies in AWS KMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/iam-policies.html"Using IAM Policies with AWS KMS/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure ECR cross-account replication to replicate the existing repository and images to all accounts in the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Cross-account replication does not support KMS re-encryption.pFor more information about ECR image replication, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/replication.html"Private Image Replication/a/span.

question_content: pA company is preparing to launch a new online store. The store's backend primarily uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and AWS Lambda. When a customer makes an order, the order details are sent to an SQS queue. A Lambda function pulls the order details from the queue and processes the order.pThe Lambda function deletes the order from the queue if the order is successfully processed. If the order is not successfully processed, the Lambda function returns an error and the message goes to a dead-letter queue.pThe company has set a 99% SLA for successful order processing for a specific time duration. The company's DevOps team needs to implement a monitoring solution that will activate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm if the SLA threshold is breached.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudWatch alarm that will calculate the rate of change of messages in the SQS queue for the time duration. Configure the alarm to go into ALARM state If the rate of change is positive.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon SQS does not process orders. The Lambda function processes orders. You must use Lambda metrics with CloudWatch to create alarms.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudWatch alarm that will go into ALARM state if there is a failed invocation of the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The company in the scenario needs an alarm that monitors the SLA threshold for a specific time duration. An alarm that enters ALARM state after a single failed invocation of the Lambda function would not meet this requirement.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudWatch alarm that will compare the number of Lambda invocations to the approximate number of messages in the SQS queue. Configure the alarm to go into ALARM state if there are 1% more Lambda invocations than the approximate number of messages in the queue.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Invocations metric reports the number of successful invocations and failed invocations. This metric does not report only the number of successful invocations. This alarm might be helpful to determine if the SQS queue is receiving more order details than the Lambda function can process, but this solution will not meet the requirements.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a CloudWatch alarm that will calculate the difference between the number of Lambda invocations and the number of Lambda errors. Configure the alarm to go into ALARM state if more than 1% of invocations are errors.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The Invocations metric reports the number of successful invocations and failed invocations. The Errors metric reports the number of invocations that result in a function error. Therefore, a CloudWatch alarm that will calculate the difference between these two metrics will meet the requirements.pFor more information about Lambda function metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/monitoring-metrics.html"Working with Lambda Function Metrics/a/span.

question_content: pA company has an application that runs on current-generation Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The EC2 instances run Amazon Linux and are launched in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. question_content: pA company uses Application Load Balancers (ALBs) as part of its application architecture. The company has ALBs in AWS accounts that are part of an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has configured AWS Config in all AWS accounts in the organization.pThe company needs to apply an AWS WAF web ACL with a common set of rules to all ALBs, including any ALBs that are created in the future. answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure AWS Firewall Manager for the organization. In the Firewall Manager administrator account, create an AWS WAF policy. Turn on automatic remediation and define the web ACL. Configure the policy scope to apply to all ALBs in the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Firewall Manager to apply AWS WAF rule groups across multiple AWS accounts. Firewall Manager policies for AWS WAF can target entire organizations, specific OUs, or a list of AWS accounts. Firewall Manager policies for AWS WAF can also target ALBs.pFor more information about Firewall Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/fms-chapter.html"AWS Firewall Manager/a/span.pFor more information about how to create a Firewall Manager policy for AWS WAF, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/create-policy.html#creating-firewall-manager-policy-for-waf"Creating an AWS Firewall Manager Policy for AWS WAF/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) from the organization's management account to enable resource sharing in the organization. Create the web ACL. Configure a resource share of the web ACL for the organization. Associate the shared web ACL with all the ALBs in the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot configure AWS RAM to share AWS WAF web ACLs. Organizations does not support the creation of AWS WAF web ACL associations. In addition, you cannot associate a web ACL with all ALBs. You must specify an individual ALB.pFor more information about which resources you can share by using AWS RAM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html"Sharable AWS Resources/a/span.pFor more information about how to associate a web ACL with an AWS resource, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl-associating-aws-resource.html"Associating or Disassociating a Web ACL with an AWS Resource/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up the ALB_WAF_ENABLED AWS Config managed rule with automatic remediation. Deploy the conformance pack to all AWS accounts in the organization.

question_content: pA company has an AWS account that contains an EC2 Image Builder pipeline that the company uses to create and test Amazon Linux golden images. In the same AWS account, the company has created a new AWS CodePipeline pipeline that packages the code for a custom Amazon EC2 agent. The final step in the CodePipeline pipeline publishes the packaged agent to an AWS CodeArtifact repository.pA DevOps engineer needs to update the Image Builder pipeline to build a new Amazon Linux golden image whenever a new version of the custom EC2 agent is created.pWhich solution will meet this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to start a new Image Builder pipeline when the agent package is published to the CodeArtifact repository. Allow the required permissions by updating the EC2 instance profile that Image Builder uses. Add a new Image Builder component that retrieves and installs the agent in the image pipeline build stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Because CodeArtifact is integrated with EventBridge, you can create rules for events and configure what happens when an event matches a rule. The EventBridge rule can invoke the Image Builder pipeline. The IAM instance profile that Image Builder uses for building and testing the AMIs should have the necessary permissions to pull the custom EC2 agent artifact from the CodeArtifact repository. The Image Builder component defines the sequence of steps that are necessary to customize an instance before image creation or to test an instance that was launched from the created image. This solution is the most operationally efficient because it uses an event-driven approach in which an action (publishing a new agent version) automatically invokes an image build.pFor more information about EventBridge events for CodeArtifact, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/working-with-service-events.html"Working with CodeArtifact Events/a/span.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to invoke Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/ev-rules-for-pipeline.html"Use EventBridge Rules with Image Builder Pipelines/a/span.pFor more information about Image Builder components, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html#image-builder-concepts"Concepts/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to start a new Image Builder pipeline when the agent package is published to the CodeArtifact repository. Allow the required permissions by updating the EC2 instance profile that Image Builder uses. Add a new Image Builder image recipe that retrieves and installs the agent in the image pipeline build stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An Image Builder image recipe is a document that defines the base image and the components that are applied to the base image to produce the desired configuration for the output AMI. You can use an image recipe to duplicate builds. However, you should use an Image Builder component to customize an instance before image creation or to test an instance that was launched from the created image. A recipe defines the whole image build, but a component defines a specific part of the image build.pFor more information about Image Builder image recipes and components, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html#image-builder-concepts"Concepts/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function that checks for new CodeArtifact package versions and starts the Image Builder pipeline if a new version exists. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function on a regular schedule. Allow the required permissions by updating the EC2 instance profile that Image Builder uses. Add a new Image Builder image recipe that retrieves and installs the agent in the image pipeline build stage.

However, this solution would not be as operationally efficient as the correct answer. The scheduled polling is unnecessary and would add an additional component to manage, monitor, and update. Additionally, the use of a recipe is incorrect. A recipe defines the whole image build, but a component defines a specific part of the image build.pFor more information about EventBridge events for CodeArtifact, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/working-with-service-events.html"Working with CodeArtifact Events/a/span.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to invoke Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/ev-rules-for-pipeline.html"Use EventBridge Rules with Image Builder Pipelines/a/span.pFor more information about Image Builder image recipes and components, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html#image-builder-concepts"Concepts/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function that checks for new CodeArtifact package versions and starts the Image Builder pipeline if a new version exists. Add a new Image Builder component that retrieves and installs the agent in the image pipeline build stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You could use a Lambda function to check CodeArtifact and to start an Image Builder pipeline. However, this solution would not be as operationally efficient as the correct answer. The scheduled polling is unnecessary and would add an additional component to manage, monitor, and update.pFor more information about EventBridge events for CodeArtifact, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/working-with-service-events.html"Working with CodeArtifact Events/a/span.pFor more information about how to use EventBridge to invoke Image Builder, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/ev-rules-for-pipeline.html"Use EventBridge Rules with Image Builder Pipelines/a/span.

question_content: pA company deploys a web application by using AWS CloudFormation. An AWS CodeCommit repository contains the CloudFormation code for the web application. Engineers push code to a staging branch, manually deploy the CloudFormation changes, and manually run integration tests against the web application.pThe company's DevOps team needs to configure a pipeline to automate the current workflow for engineers. This solution is the most operationally efficient because all the services have native integrations with the required actions.pFor more information about how to build a pipeline for test and production stacks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/continuous-delivery-codepipeline-basic-walkthrough.html"Walkthrough: Building a Pipeline for Test and Production Stacks/a/span.pFor more information about CodeBuild test report groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/test-report-group.html"Working with Report Groups/a/span.

Configure a pipeline deploy stage to deploy a new web application CloudFormation stack. Configure a pipeline test stage that uses AWS CodeBuild to run the integration tests and export the test results in a supported test report file format. Publish the tests results to the new CodeArtifact repository.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new Amazon S3 bucket to host the test results. Configure a new AWS CodePipeline pipeline that starts when the CodeCommit repository staging branch is updated. question_content: pA company is migrating Docker repositories to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) in an existing AWS account. A DevOps engineer needs to automate the management of images that are uploaded to the repositories. The solution must limit the number of image versions. As a first step, the DevOps engineer creates a private repository in Amazon ECR for each repository that the company will migrate.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

Schedule the Lambda function to run automatically at regular intervals.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The configuration of a Lambda function is not the most operationally efficient solution because you would need to maintain extra code. Additionally, you would need to create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function.pFor more information about Lambda, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html"What Is AWS Lambda?/a/spanpFor more information about how to use EventBridge to schedule Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html"Tutorial: Schedule AWS Lambda Functions Using EventBridge/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a repository policy that assesses the number of images and deletes older versions if the number of images is greater than the desired number of images. Apply the repository policy to each private repository.

You can define which IAM users or roles have access to a repository policy, but repository policies do not delete older versions of images.pFor more information about ECR repository policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html"Private Repository Policies/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Step Functions state machine Express Workflow to scan the images in each repository for the number of versions present. answer_choices.choice_content: pPush an image into each private repository. This solution meets the requirements in the most operationally efficient manner because Amazon ECR provides this automation as a feature.pFor more information about ECR lifecycle policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/LifecyclePolicies.html"Lifecycle Policies/a/span.pFor more information about how to create a lifecycle policy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/lp_creation.html"Creating a Lifecycle Policy/a/span.

question_content: pA company has configured AWS CodeDeploy to automatically update an AWS Lambda application. The deployment has failed a few times recently. A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution to immediately notify the company's application team by email when failures occur in the future.pThe DevOps engineer creates an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for failed deployments.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the notification requirement in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send a message to the SNS topic when a deployment state changes to the failed deployment state. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would involve the configuration of CloudWatch logs to send a notification when an alarm is invoked because of a failed deployment. CodeDeploy cannot directly send logs to CloudWatch. You can send CodeDeploy agent metric data and log data to CloudWatch by using the unified CloudWatch agent. However, this process would require more operational overhead.pFor more information about AWS services that publish logs to CloudWatch Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/aws-services-sending-logs.html"AWS Services that Publish Logs to CloudWatch Logs/a/span.pFor more information about how to send CodeDeploy agent logs to CloudWatch, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/codedeploy-agent-operations-cloudwatch-agent.html"Send CodeDeploy Agent Logs to CloudWatch/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTurn on AWS CloudTrail logging in the company's AWS account. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Subscribe the queue to the SNS topic. Use the queue to send the email notification.

This solution would publish notifications for all the CloudTrail logs to the SNS topic instead of publishing only notifications for the logs that are related to a failed deployment. The queue cannot be used to send the email notifications.pFor more information about how to configure SNS notifications for CloudTrail, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/configure-sns-notifications-for-cloudtrail.html"Configuring Amazon SNS Notifications for CloudTrail/a/span.pFor more information about how to monitor deployments with SNS event notifications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-event-notifications.html"Monitoring Deployments with Amazon SNS Event Notifications/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn CodeDeploy, create a trigger for failed deployments. Specify the SNS topic as the destination. Subscribe the application team's email address to the SNS topic.

The application team's email address can be a subscriber to the SNS topic. This built-in mechanism within CodeDeploy is operationally efficient because the mechanism does not involve any additional AWS resources.pFor more information about how to create an invocation for a CodeDeploy event, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/monitoring-sns-event-notifications-create-trigger.html"Create a Trigger for a CodeDeploy Event/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIn CodeDeploy, create a trigger for failed deployments. Specify the SNS topic as the destination. Create a Lambda function that sends an email message when an event is published to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The DevOps engineer in the scenario could use a Lambda function to process notifications asynchronously. question_content: pA company has a security group that is associated with Amazon EC2 instances. Configure the EventBridge rule to target the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team.

However, the EC2 Instance State-change Notification event pattern does not detect any changes in security group rules.pFor more information about state change events for EC2 instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-instance-state-changes.html"State Change Events for Your Instances/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Config custom rule that is compliant if the security group rule for 192.168.1.5/32 for HTTPS/443 is present in the inbound rules of the security group. Configure AWS Config to target the SNS topic to notify the SecOps team if the AWS Config rule is noncompliant.

However, the rule does not check the rules of the security group.pFor more information about the ec2-security-group-attached-to-eni-periodic AWS Config managed rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ec2-security-group-attached-to-eni-periodic.html"ec2-security-group-attached-to-eni-periodic/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses the AWS API Call via CloudTrail event type. question_content: pA company has an AWS account that includes Amazon S3 buckets in the us-west-2 Region. The company has configured AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config for us-west-2. question_content: pA company publishes application logs to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group in the us-east-1 Region. The company needs to export the logs from us-east-1 to the us-west-2 Region on a weekly basis. The logs must be encrypted in both Regions.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket in us-west-2. Configure server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for the S3 bucket. Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The S3 bucket must exist in the same Region as the log group.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket in us-west-2. Configure server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the S3 bucket. Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The default bucket encryption must be SSE-S3, not SSE-KMS. Additionally, the S3 bucket must be in the same Region as the log group.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Create an S3 bucket in us-west-2. Configure server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) and turn on versioning for both S3 buckets. Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure a replication rule on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate the logs to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can export CloudWatch logs to an S3 bucket. This process requires that the default bucket encryption is SSE-S3. Additionally, the S3 bucket must be in the same Region as the log group. S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) can copy the logs to the required S3 bucket in a different Region.pFor more information about how to export CloudWatch logs to Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3Export.html" tabindex="-1"Exporting log data to Amazon S3/a/span. pFor more information about how to use the AWS CLI to export log data, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/S3ExportTasks.html" tabindex="-1"Export log data to Amazon S3 using the AWS CLI/a/span.pFor more information about replication of S3 objects, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html" tabindex="-1"Replicating objects/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Create an S3 bucket in us-west-2. Configure server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) and turn on versioning for both S3 buckets. Create and schedule an AWS Lambda function to run weekly to export the CloudWatch logs from the last week to the S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure a replication rule on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate the logs to the S3 bucket in us-west-2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The default bucket encryption must be SSE-S3, not SSE-KMS.pFor more information about replication of S3 objects, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html" tabindex="-1"Replicating objects/a/span.

question_content: pA company is using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate data from a source database in a data center to a target Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. The company has created a DMS replication task with change data capture (CDC).pThe replication instance sometimes gets interrupted and affects critical functionality. The company must improve the replication instance's resiliency and receive notifications about interruptions.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCopy data from the source database to Amazon S3 by using AWS DataSync. Configure AWS Lambda functions to copy the data to the target database. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the Lambda functions for errors and throttles. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DataSync is an online data transfer service that simplifies, automates, and accelerates the movement of data between storage systems and services. However, the source database cannot be the source location in DataSync. Additionally, Lambda functions would be limited by compute capacity and invocation time.pFor more information about DataSync, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html"What is AWS DataSync?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor DMS replication task metrics and host metrics. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to configure a standby DMS replication instance in a different AWS Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In AWS DMS, you can use replication task and instance metrics to monitor for failures. A standby DMS replication instance would improve availability. However, the replication instance in another Region would require you to create a new DMS replication task. This solution would add unnecessary operational overhead by involving another Region and by creating a Lambda function. This solution also could cause duplicate records or primary key violation errors.pFor more information about how to monitor DMS tasks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Monitoring.html"Monitoring AWS DMS tasks/a/span.pFor more information about replication instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.Creating.html"Creating a replication instance/a/span.pFor more information about errors in AWS DMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Troubleshooting.html"Troubleshooting migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor DMS replication task metrics and host metrics. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification. After receiving the notification, configure a new DMS replication task in the same AWS Region.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. In AWS DMS, you can use replication task and instance metrics to monitor for failures. A new DMS replication instance would improve availability. However, to create the replication instance, you would need to create a new DMS replication task. This solution would add unnecessary operational overhead by involving manual configuration. This solution also could cause duplicate records or primary key violation errors.pFor more information about how to monitor DMS tasks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Monitoring.html"Monitoring AWS DMS tasks/a/span.pFor more information about replication instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.Creating.html"Creating a replication instance/a/span.pFor more information about errors in AWS DMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Troubleshooting.html"Troubleshooting migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the DMS replication instance by turning on Multi-AZ support. Create Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor DMS replication task metrics and host metrics. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. In AWS DMS, you can modify the existing replication instance by turning on Multi-AZ support. Multi-AZ support creates a standby replica of the replication instance in another Availability Zone for failover. This solution provides high availability with the least operational overhead. Additionally, you can use replication task and instance metrics to monitor for failures. Amazon SNS can provide the notifications.pFor more information about how to monitor DMS tasks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Monitoring.html"Monitoring AWS DMS tasks/a/span.pFor more information about how to modify replication instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.Modifying.html"Modifying a replication instance/a/span.pFor more information about the DMS maintenance window, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_ReplicationInstance.MaintenanceWindow.html"Working with the AWS DMS maintenance window/a/span.

question_content: pA company has deployed an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The company must implement an automated deployment strategy that ensures zero downtime without affecting the application's performance.pWhich deployment strategy will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure rate controls for the automation. Specify a concurrency value of 100% and an error threshold of 1 error.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an Automation runbook to automate a variety of operations on managed instances and other AWS resources. An Automation runbook with support actions can deploy application revisions on EC2 instances. However, with concurrency set to 100%, the runbook would implement deployment on all instances immediately and would introduce downtime.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-actions.html" tabindex="-1"Systems Manager Automation actions reference/a/span.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation rate controls, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/running-automations-scale-controls.html" tabindex="-1"Control automations at scale/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an application in AWS CodeDeploy. Create a deployment group and specify the in-place deployment type. Configure CodeDeploy to automatically deploy the application revision to the Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2 instances, on-premises instances, AWS Lambda functions, or Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) tasks. A deployment group with an in-place deployment type can implement deployment in a linear fashion on the existing EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group. This type of deployment could affect the application's availability.pFor more information about in-place deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html#welcome-deployment-overview-in-place" tabindex="-1"Overview of an in-place deployment/a/span.pFor more information about EC2 in-place deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html#deployment-configuration-server" tabindex="-1"Deployment configurations on an EC2/on-premises compute platform/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an application in AWS CodeDeploy. Create a deployment group and specify the blue/green deployment type. Configure CodeDeploy to automatically copy the Auto Scaling group for the replacement environment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2 instances, on-premises instances, AWS Lambda functions, or Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) tasks. A deployment group with a blue/green deployment type and a setting to copy an existing Auto Scaling group creates new instances for the replacement environment during the deployment. When new instances are launched with the newer revision, the traffic will be routed to one instance in the replacement environment at a time. If the deployment fails, rollback can occur immediately because of the blue/green deployment. This solution will ensure zero downtime without affecting the application's performance.pFor more information about in-place deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html#welcome-deployment-overview-in-place" tabindex="-1"Overview of an in-place deployment/a/span.pFor more information about EC2 in-place deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html#deployment-configuration-server" tabindex="-1"Deployment configurations on an EC2/on-premises compute platform/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure rate controls for the automation. Specify a concurrency value of 50% and an error threshold of 1 error.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an Automation runbook to automate a variety of operations on managed instances and other AWS resources. An Automation runbook with support actions can deploy application revisions on EC2 instances. However, with concurrency set to 50%, the runbook will implement deployment on half of the existing instances immediately. This solution would direct the user traffic to the remaining instances and would affect the application's performance.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-actions.html" tabindex="-1"Systems Manager Automation actions reference/a/span.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation rate controls, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/running-automations-scale-controls.html" tabindex="-1"Control automations at scale/a/span.

question_content: pA company needs to migrate a legacy internal web application from its on-premises data center to its AWS account. The company already has configured a VPC that has two public subnets and two private subnets. The VPC has outbound internet connectivity.pThe application can run on only a single server at a time. Other existing on-premises applications need to communicate with the migrated application. Create a launch template to install the legacy application on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses the launch template. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The ALB in the public subnets provides the entry point of the application. When an EC2 instance starts, the instance uses the user data that is defined in the launch template to configure the legacy application.pFor more information about ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html"What is an Application Load Balancer?/a/spanpFor more information about how to create ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-application-load-balancer.html"Create an Application Load Balancer/a/span.pFor more information about launch templates, see a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/launch-templates.html"span style="text-decoration: underline;"Launch templates/span/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is associated with the private subnets in the VPC. Create a launch template to install the legacy application on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses the launch template. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The ALB needs to be in public subnets to be addressable over the internet by the on-premises applications.pFor more information about ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html"What is an Application Load Balancer?/a/spanpFor more information about how to create ALBs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-application-load-balancer.html"Create an Application Load Balancer/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule that allows traffic from the company's on-premises data center. Associate the web ACL with the Application Load Balancer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An AWS WAF web ACL can make the Application Load Balancer accessible only by the on-premises applications.pFor more information about AWS WAF web ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html"Using AWS WAF to control access to your content/a/span.pFor more information about the IP set match rule statement, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-ipset-match.html"IP set match rule statement/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule that denies traffic from the company's on-premises data center. Associate the web ACL with the Application Load Balancer.

Traffic from the on-premises data center to the migrated application needs to be allowed, not denied.pFor more information about AWS WAF web ACLs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/distribution-web-awswaf.html"Using AWS WAF to control access to your content/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the Auto Scaling group capacity limits to have a minimum capacity of 1, a maximum capacity of 1, and a desired capacity of 1.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. With the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity, maximum capacity, and desired capacity set to 1, the application meets the requirement to run on only a single instance at a time.pFor more information about capacity limits for Auto Scaling groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-capacity-limits.html"Set capacity limits on your Auto Scaling group/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the Auto Scaling group capacity limits to have a minimum capacity of 2, a maximum capacity of 3, and a desired capacity of 2.
