question_content: pA company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk by using an all-at-once deployment method. The deployment failed recently because of an application misconfiguration and resulted in significant downtime.pTo prevent such downtime in the future, a DevOps engineer needs to revise the deployment method while maintaining the application performance. The DevOps engineer must ensure that application versions are consistently configured across all instances without creating new environments.pWhich deployment solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSwitch to a rolling deployment strategy for future application updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A rolling deployment would update one or more instances at a time to replace the current application. This solution would eliminate downtime during an update. However, with fewer instances available during the deployment, this solution would not necessarily maintain the same application performance. Additionally, when deployment failures occur, the application would not be consistent across all instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSwitch to a rolling deployment with additional batch strategy for future application updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A rolling deployment with additional batch strategy would deploy new instances and would update one or more instances at a time to replace the current application. This solution would eliminate downtime during an update. With additional instances available during the deployment, this solution also would maintain the same application performance. However, deployment failure in the middle of the deployment process could lead to instances that have an older version of the application and instances that have the new version of the application.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSwitch to an immutable deployment strategy for future application updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An immutable deployment would launch a full set of new instances that run the new application. This solution would eliminate downtime and would maintain the same application performance. Additionally, the deployment of the application update would be consistent on all the new instances. New instances must pass health checks before they are used to serve traffic. When the new systems are running and healthy, the original instances are removed.pFor more information about deployment policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.deploy-existing-version.html" tabindex="-1"Deploying applications to Elastic Beanstalk environments/a/span.pFor more information about the implementation of deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.rolling-version-deploy.html" tabindex="-1"Deployment policies and settings/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSwitch to a blue/green deployment strategy for future application updates.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A blue/green deployment would violate the company's requirement to avoid the creation of new environments. This solution would require the creation of an entire new environment in Elastic Beanstalk. You could swap the old environment endpoint with a new environment endpoint. This solution would eliminate downtime and maintain the same application performance. However, this solution would leave both the original environment and the new environment running.pFor more information about blue/green deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.CNAMESwap.html" tabindex="-1"Blue/Green deployments with Elastic Beanstalk/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses AWS CloudFormation to manage an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The instances are in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The company wants to treat its infrastructure as immutable.pA DevOps engineer must implement a solution to replace two EC2 instances at a time whenever operating system configuration updates are needed or when new Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are needed. A minimum of four EC2 instances must be running whenever an update is in progress.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the CloudFormation template to include an UpdatePolicy attribute for the Auto Scaling group. Include the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy with MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. UpdatePolicy is a minor addition to an existing AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup resource. MinInstancesInService guarantees a minimum number of instances during the update, regardless of the capacity setting on the Auto Scaling group. MaxBatchSize controls the number of instances added or removed at a time. CloudFormation detects whenever a change set includes a new launch template version and automatically performs a blue/green update. You can modify the launch template's ImageId or UserData by using template parameters.pFor more information about UpdatePolicy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html#cfn-attributes-updatepolicy-rollingupdate"AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has an in-place deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy with an in-place deployment type performs mutable updates on EC2 instances. These updates are software updates. This solution does not update AMIs and does not replace EC2 instances.pFor more information about CodeDeploy deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html"Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to 4. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group that has a blue/green deployment type. Select Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group for the environment configuration. Whenever a new revision is available, create a new CodeDeploy deployment that has a deployment configuration of CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy with a blue/green deployment type performs immutable updates by replacing the existing EC2 instances with new EC2 instances. These updates are software updates. This solution does not update AMIs.pFor more information about blue/green deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html#welcome-deployment-overview-blue-green"Overview of a blue/green deployment/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the CloudFormation template to include a StackPolicy. Designate an AutoScalingReplacingUpdate policy to control the update. Specify MinInstancesInService of 4 and MaxBatchSize of 2. Whenever a software update is needed, alter either or both of the ImageId and UserData of the AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate and update the stack.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. StackPolicy is a property of a CloudFormation stack, not an element of a template. A stack policy prevents stack resources from being unintentionally updated or deleted during a stack update. A stack policy does not control specific update behaviors on resources. AutoScalingReplacingUpdate is an UpdatePolicy strategy, not part of a StackPolicy. AutoScalingReplacingUpdate replaces an existing Auto Scaling group with another Auto Scaling group. AutoScalingReplacingUpdate has no ability to control minimum instances in service or batch size.pFor more information about StackPolicy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuiderotect-stack-resources.html"Prevent updates to stack resources/a/span.pFor more information about AutoScalingReplacingUpdate, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-updatepolicy.html#cfn-attributes-updatepolicy-replacingupdate"AutoScalingReplacing update policy/a/span.

question_content: pA company is running an application on Amazon EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer needs to aggregate the application logs to a central system for the company's application team to search. A critical error message periodically appears in the log files. The DevOps engineer needs to notify the application team by email when these error messages occur.pWhich solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to publish the application logs files to a CloudWatch log group. Configure a metric filter on the CloudWatch log group to detect the critical errors and to create a custom metric. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team’s email address to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can configure the unified CloudWatch agent to publish log files to a CloudWatch log group. In the log group, you can define filter patterns to detect the error message and to create a custom metric. You can use this metric to activate alarms that can send notifications by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).pFor more information about how to configure the CloudWatch agent, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html"Collect metrics and logs from Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers with the CloudWatch agent/a/span.pFor more information about how to create a metric filter for a log group, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html"Create a metric filter for a log group/a/span.pFor more information about CloudWatch alarms, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/AlarmThatSendsEmail.html"Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the Amazon Kinesis agent on the EC2 instances. Configure the Kinesis agent with the location of the log files. Stream the logs to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with an Amazon CloudWatch metrics stream as a destination. Configure an AWS Lambda function to detect the error message and to create a custom metric. Associate the Lambda function with the stream. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team’s email address to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can install the Kinesis agent on EC2 instances and can configure the agent to stream each entry of specified log files to a delivery stream. However, Kinesis Data Firehose cannot stream to a CloudWatch metrics stream. Additionally, the stream's Lambda function cannot filter the stream.pFor more information about Kinesis Data Firehose destinations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html"Destination Settings/a/span.pFor more information about how to use Lambda with Kinesis Data Firehose, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesisfirehose.html"Using AWS Lambda with Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pInstall the AWS X-Ray daemon on the EC2 instances. Instrument the application with the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT). Configure the ADOT collector with the location of the custom log files and the name of an Amazon CloudWatch log group. Use the CloudWatch embedded metric format to generate a custom metric that is based on the error message. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to use the custom metric to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team’s email address to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. X-Ray is a service that collects data about requests that an application serves. X-Ray provides no support for collecting or streaming logs to a central repository. ADOT gives an application the ability to participate in tracing without code changes. The embedded metric format is not usable with an application's log output.pFor more information about X-Ray, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html"What is AWS X-Ray?/a/spanpFor more information about ADOT, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-instrumenting-your-app.html#xray-instrumenting-opentel"Instrumenting your application with the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to publish the application logs files to a CloudWatch log group. Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Subscribe the CloudWatch log group to the OpenSearch Service domain. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an OpenSearch Service alert monitor to notify the SNS topic. Subscribe the application team’s email address to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This option is not the most operationally efficient solution because of the overhead that is associated with an OpenSearch Service domain.pFor more information about how to stream CloudWatch Logs data to OpenSearch Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_OpenSearch_Stream.html"Streaming CloudWatch Logs data to Amazon OpenSearch Service/a/span.pFor more information about how to configure alerts in OpenSearch Service, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/alerting.html"Configuring alerts in Amazon OpenSearch Service/a/span.

question_content: pA DevOps engineer has created an AWS CodeCommit repository for a team of software developers. The developers want to use their existing SSH keys to access the repository from Linux development workstations.pWhich combination of steps will allow the developers to use Git to pull and push with this repository? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pAttach an IAM policy to each developer's IAM account with CodeCommit:GitPush and CodeCommit:GitPull permissions on the repository resource.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. All actions are denied unless they are explicitly allowed in the AWS Cloud. You must attach an IAM policy to each IAM user to define the user's permissions within CodeCommit. The permissions include GitPush, GitPull, and potentially other actions.pFor more information about how to use IAM policies for CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-identity-based-access-control.html"Using identity-based policies (IAM Policies) for CodeCommit/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpload each developer's SSH public key to their IAM user security credentials tab.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can associate security credentials with an IAM user. You must upload an IAM user's SSH public key to their security credentials to allow key-based Git access.For more information about the configuration of SSH keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/setting-up-ssh-unixes.html#setting-up-ssh-unixes-keys"Step 3: Configure credentials on Linux, macOS, or Unix/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd each developer's IAM access key to their .ssh/authorized_keys file.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The .ssh/authorized_key file specifies users that are allowed to use SSH to connect to the host where the file is located. In this case, the host would be the developer's computer, not the CodeCommit repository.pFor more information about SSH keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-key-pairs.html"Amazon EC2 key pairs and Linux instances/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate each developer's .ssh/known_hosts file with the correct values for Host, User, and IdentityFile.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The developers must update their .ssh/config file (not the .ssh/known_hosts file) with the correct values for Host, User, and IdentityFile to establish an SSH connection. The known_hosts file is used to detect fingerprint changes in hosts to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.pFor more information about SSH, see href="https://www.ssh.com/ssh/host-key#sec-Known-Host-Keys"SSH Host Key - What, Why, How/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun the aws configure command to add each developer's access key ID and secret access key for API access.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You run the aws configure command from the command line to set up AWS credentials to access the AWS APIs. The developers are using Git and do not use API access to pull and push code from a CodeCommit repository. The developers use the SSH keys.pFor more information about the aws configure command, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-quickstart.html"Configuration basics/a/span. pFor more information about the configuration of SSH keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/setting-up-ssh-unixes.html#setting-up-ssh-unixes-keys"Step 3: Configure credentials on Linux, macOS, or Unix/a/span. pFor more information about how to use IAM policies for CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/auth-and-access-control-iam-identity-based-access-control.html"Using identity-based policies for CodeCommit/a/span.

question_content: pA manufacturing company stores all of its telemetry data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. After the data is written, the items do not change. To reduce storage costs, the company must archive all data for the long term. However, data that is less than 60 days old must be available to applications.pWhich combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to move data into archival storage MOST cost-effectively? (Select THREE.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable TTL on the table. Assign an attribute that contains a timestamp 60 days in the future. Make that attribute a TTL attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The configuration of TTL will delete old items from the table.pFor more information about DynamoDB TTL, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/howitworks-ttl.html"How It Works: DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL)/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable point-in-time recovery on the table. Set the recovery window for 60 days.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Point-in-time recovery is not an archival solution because it retains the data for only 35 days. There is no mechanism to set the retention period for 60 days.pFor more information about point-in-time recovery, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguideointInTimeRecovery_Howitworks.html"Point-in-Time Recovery: How It Works/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to create daily on-demand backups of the table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DynamoDB on-demand backups are less cost-effective than S3 Glacier Deep Archive. Additionally, each backup is a full backup.pFor more information about DynamoDB on-demand backups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/BackupRestore.html"On-Demand Backup and Restore for DynamoDB/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable DynamoDB Streams on the table. Create an AWS Lambda function to poll the DynamoDB stream. Deliver the records to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You need a Lambda function to poll the DynamoDB stream and write to Kinesis Data Firehose.pFor more information about archiving items to Amazon S3 by using DynamoDB TTL with Lambda and Kinesis Data Firehose, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/automatically-archive-items-to-s3-using-dynamodb-time-to-live-with-aws-lambda-and-amazon-kinesis-firehose/"Automatically Archive Items to S3 using DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) with AWS Lambda and Amazon Kinesis Firehose/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable DynamoDB Streams on the table. Configure Amazon EventBridge to emit an event for table writes. Configure the event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to capture the new data. Write the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. EventBridge cannot directly detect DynamoDB events such as table writes. EventBridge would provide only metrics. A Lambda invocation that is based on table writes would not be possible with this solution.pFor more information about archiving items to Amazon S3 by using DynamoDB TTL with Lambda and Kinesis Data Firehose, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/automatically-archive-items-to-s3-using-dynamodb-time-to-live-with-aws-lambda-and-amazon-kinesis-firehose/"Automatically Archive Items to S3 using DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) with AWS Lambda and Amazon Kinesis Firehose/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Set S3 Lifecycle policies on the S3 bucket to archive the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after zero days.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is cold storage and is the least expensive available storage for archives. This step is the final step in setting the archival strategy.pFor more information about S3 Glacier, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonglacier/latest/dev/introduction.html"What Is Amazon S3 Glacier?/a/span

question_content: pA company is implementing a CI/CD pipeline with a workflow-driven action that includes a step that must wait for data to be imported from the data science team's infrastructure. This data import task runs on an Amazon EC2 instance and can take up to 60 minutes to finish running. A DevOps engineer must implement a pipeline that minimizes the maintenance burden on the data science team.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up a Jenkins build server on an EC2 instance. Use a Jenkins Pipeline plugin to orchestrate the continuous integration process. Use the Jenkins Pipeline plugin to call a shell script to run the data import. Determine the next stage based on the output of the script.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can set up a CI/CD pipeline by using Jenkins on an EC2 instance. However, this solution does not minimize the maintenance burden on the data science team. The team would be responsible for the maintenance of the EC2 instance and the Jenkins installation. A fully managed service such as CodePipeline would reduce maintenance.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CodePipeline to set up build and deployment steps for the CI/CD pipeline. For the data import from the data science team, set up an action that invokes an AWS Step Functions state machine by using an activity task for the data import step that runs on Amazon EC2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodePipeline works as the CI/CD pipeline that orchestrates the build and deployment steps. CodePipeline integrates with Step Functions. The use of fully managed services such as CodePipeline minimizes the maintenance burden.pFor more information about integration between CodePipeline and Step Functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-StepFunctions.html"AWS Step Functions/a/span. pFor more information about CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What is AWS CodePipeline?/a/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CodeBuild to set up the CI/CD pipeline and convert the data transfer task that runs on Amazon EC2 to run on an AWS Lambda function. Invoke the Lambda function with an Amazon CloudWatch Logs event to import the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can set up a Lambda function to run based on a CloudWatch Logs filter. However, the Lambda function has a maximum runtime of 15 minutes. This time limit would prevent the completion of the data import step. Additionally, CodeBuild can build the code, but CodeBuild does not account for the code deployment requirement of the CI/CD pipeline.pFor more information about Lambda and CloudWatch Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html#LambdaFunctionExample"Example 2: Subscription filters with AWS Lambda/a/span.pFor more information about the Lambda function timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html"Lambda quotas/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CodePipeline to send a call that invokes an AWS Lambda function instead of Amazon EC2 to run the data import step. Configure the Lambda function to return a custom JSON event and a response code 200 when the step is ready to proceed. Rely on CodePipeline to evaluate the result and determine the next steps.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CodePipeline to orchestrate the CI/CD pipeline. However, the Lambda function has a maximum runtime of 15 minutes. This time limit would prevent the completion of the data import step.pFor more information about the Lambda function timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html"Lambda quotas/a/span. pFor more information about CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What is AWS CodePipeline?/a/span.

question_content: pA company is deploying a web application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. A DevOps engineer needs to implement a process to automatically run a bash script on each Amazon EC2 instance in the environment after the application is deployed.pWhat should the DevOps engineer do to meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a .config file with a commands section. Include each command in the bash script as one entry in the commands section. Place the .config file within the .ebextensions directory in the application bundle.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Instructions within commands run before the application has been extracted and deployed. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement to run the script after the application is deployed.pFor more information about commands, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/customize-containers-ec2.html#linux-commands"Commands/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a .config file with a container_commands section. Include each command in the bash script as one entry in the container_commands section. Place the .config file within the .ebextensions directory in the application bundle.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Container commands run after the application has been extracted, but before the application is deployed to the final location. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement to run the script after the application is deployed.pFor more information about container commands, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/customize-containers-ec2.html#linux-container-commands"Container commands/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a .config file with a files section. In the files section, write the contents of the bash script to a script file in the post hooks directory within appdeploy. Place the .config file within the .ebextensions directory in the application bundle.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. When an instance is launched, Elastic Beanstalk runs preinit, appdeploy, and postinit, in this order. On subsequent deployments to running instances, Elastic Beanstalk runs appdeploy hooks. In this use case, the placement of a script within appdeploy by using the files section of .ebextensions will meet the requirement.pFor more information about files, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/customize-containers-ec2.html#linux-files"Files/a/span. pFor more information about custom platform hooks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/custom-platform-hooks.html"Custom platform hooks/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the Elastic Beanstalk console or CLI to provide a custom AMI with the user data for the EC2 instances in the environment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The user data will run when the EC2 instance is started. However, this solution does not ensure that the user data script will run after the application has been deployed to its final location and is up and running.pFor more information about the use of custom AMIs with Elastic Beanstalk, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.customenv.html"Using a custom Amazon machine image (AMI)/a/span.

question_content: pAn ecommerce company is looking for ways to deploy an application on AWS that satisfies the following requirements:ulliHas a simple and automated application deployment process./liliHas minimal deployment costs while ensuring that at least half of the instances are available to receive end-user requests./liliIf the application fails, an automated healing mechanism will replace the affected instances./li/ulpWhich deployment strategy will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment and configure it to use Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use rolling deployments with a batch size of 50%.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Elastic Beanstalk will not automatically replace instances where the application has failed. By default, Elastic Beanstalk will use the Elastic Load Balancer's standard TCP health check. Therefore, this strategy does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about Elastic Beanstalk health checks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.healthstatus.html#using-features.healthstatus.understanding"Elastic Load Balancing Health Checks/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS OpsWorks stack. Configure the application layer to use rolling deployments as a deployment strategy. Add an Elastic Load Balancing layer. Enable auto healing on the application layer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Auto healing will not replace instances in response to the application status. Instead, auto healing replaces instances only if the OpsWorks Stacks agent is not able to communicate with the service. Therefore, this strategy does not meet the requirements.pFor more information about OpsWorks Stacks auto healing, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opsworks/latest/userguide/workinginstances-autohealing.html"Using Auto Healing to Replace Failed Instances/a/span.pFor more information about the OpsWorks Stacks agent, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opsworks/latest/userguide/agent.html"AWS OpsWorks Stacks Agent CLI/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use the CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime deployment strategy. Enable an Elastic Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime deployment configuration ensures that 50% of the instances are available during deployment. By setting Auto Scaling to ELB, you ensure that an instance will be replaced if the Elastic Load Balancing health check fails.pFor more information about deployment configurations in CodeDeploy, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-configurations.html"Working with Deployment Configurations in CodeDeploy/a/span.pFor more information about Elastic Load Balancing health checks and Auto Scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-elb-healthcheck.html"Add Elastic Load Balancing Health Checks to an Auto Scaling Group/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CodeDeploy with Auto Scaling and an Elastic Load Balancer. Use a blue/green deployment strategy. Enable an Elastic Load Balancing health check to report the status of the application, and set the Auto Scaling health check to ELB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A blue/green deployment strategy will not meet the requirement of having 50% of instances available. A blue/green deployment involves two separate but identical environments. One environment (blue) runs the current application version, and the other environment (green) runs the new application version.pFor more information about how blue/green deployments shift traffic, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments.html"Working with Deployments in CodeDeploy/a/span.pFor more information about blue/green deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/overview-deployment-options/bluegreen-deployments.html"Blue/Green Deployments/a/span.

question_content: pA company manages multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. A DevOps engineer must ensure that all IAM entity configurations across these accounts are compliant with corporate IAM policies.pWhich combination of steps will accomplish this goal? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pActivate AWS Security Hub in the organization's management account. Configure Security Hub to report on all corporate IAM policy violations.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security state in the AWS Cloud and helps check your environment against security industry standards and best practices. Security Hub does not support the creation of a report about the state of custom AWS Config rules.pFor more information about Security Hub standards and controls, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-standards.html"Security Standards and Controls in AWS Security Hub/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an AWS Config aggregator in the organization's management account for all accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Config offers multi-account and multi-Region aggregation of configuration and compliance data.pFor more information about AWS Config data aggregation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/aggregate-data.html"Multi-Account Multi-Region Data Aggregation/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFrom the organization's management account, activate AWS IAM Access Analyzer in all accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. IAM Access Analyzer helps to identify the resources in your organization and accounts, such as Amazon S3 buckets or IAM roles, that are shared with an external entity. IAM Access Analyzer does not enforce policy.pFor more information about IAM Access Analyzer, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html"Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFrom AWS Security Hub in the organization's management account, add all accounts in the organization as Security Hub member accounts.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Security Hub provides a comprehensive view of your security state in the AWS Cloud and helps check your environment against security industry standards and best practices. Security Hub does not support the creation of a report about the state of custom AWS Config rules.pFor more information about Security Hub standards and controls, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-standards.html"Security Standards and Controls in AWS Security Hub/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy AWS Config rules that match the corporate IAM policies to all accounts in the organization.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can deploy AWS Config rules across all accounts in the organization and then aggregate the data.pFor more information about how to manage AWS Config rules across all accounts, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/config-rule-multi-account-deployment.html"Managing AWS Config Rules across All Accounts in Your Organization/a/span.pFor more information about AWS Config data aggregation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/aggregate-data.html"Multi-Account Multi-Region Data Aggregation/a/span.

question_content: pA company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host applications for its customers. Recently, the company's support team has received EC2 scheduled maintenance notifications regarding its EC2 instances.pThe support team wants to automatically perform a restart of any EC2 instances with a scheduled maintenance event before the scheduled date.pWhich solution will meet these requirements while requiring the MINIMUM amount of development effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Systems Manager maintenance window with a Systems Manager Automation task that uses the RebootInstances EC2 API operation to restart the affected EC2 instances. Attach the EC2 instances to the maintenance window. Configure AWS Health to invoke the maintenance window whenever a scheduledChange event for Amazon EC2 is generated.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot configure AWS Health to perform actions, and AWS Health cannot invoke Systems Manager. Additionally, each maintenance window has a schedule and cannot be invoked by other services.pFor more information about supported operations in AWS Health, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/supported-operations.html"Supported Operations in AWS Health/a/span.pFor more information about supported task types in Systems Manager Maintenance Windows, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-maintenance.html"AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed metric of each EC2 instance. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to recover any affected EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch alarms can detect underlying hardware failures but not scheduled maintenance events. Additionally, you must set up an alarm action to recover the EC2 instances.pFor more information about available EC2 instance checks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-system-instance-status-check.html#types-of-instance-status-checks"Types of Status Checks/a/span.pFor more information about how to create alarms to recover EC2 instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/UsingAlarmActions.html"Create Alarms to Stop, Terminate, Reboot, or Recover an EC2 Instance/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches scheduledChange events for Amazon EC2 from AWS Health. Configure the rule to run the AWS-RestartEC2Instance AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Health sends scheduledChange events that EventBridge can capture and use to invoke Systems Manager. The AWS-RestartEC2Instance runbook replaces the need for custom code implementation. This solution uses managed services entirely and requires minimal development effort.pFor more information about the integration between EventBridge and AWS Health, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/cloudwatch-events-health.html"Monitoring AWS Health Events with Amazon EventBridge/a/span.pFor more information about runbooks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-runbook-reference.html"Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches scheduledChange events for Amazon EC2 from AWS Health. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the EC2 API to list all EC2 instances with scheduled events and then uses the RebootInstances EC2 API operation to restart the affected EC2 instances. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution would work, but it requires more development effort than the correct answer requires. The additional effort in this solution comes from the creation of the Lambda function with custom code to call the EC2 API.pFor more information about the integration between EventBridge and AWS Health, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/health/latest/ug/cloudwatch-events-health.html"Monitoring AWS Health Events with Amazon EventBridge/a/span.pFor more information about how to call the RebootInstances EC2 API operation, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_RebootInstances.html"RebootInstances/a/span.

question_content: pA DevOps team wants to use AWS CodeBuild to build a Java application and package the application in a Docker container image. The resulting image must be tagged with a value that corresponds to a simple incrementing version number. The image must be pushed to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up the CodeBuild project with the latest aws/codebuild/standard image and no output artifact. Use the ECR get-login-password command to obtain a password to the ECR repository. Use this value in the Docker login command. Use the CODEBUILD_BUILD_NUMBER variable and Docker tag commands to tag the image with the fully qualified ECR repository name and build number.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeBuild standard images have Java and Docker preinstalled. A project that produces a Docker image produces no other Amazon S3 output. The Docker login command is necessary to authenticate with Amazon ECR. The get-login-password command is a way to acquire ECR login credentials. CodeBuild provides several environment variables that you can use to obtain a sequential build number from the underlying commit. Docker images that you push to Amazon ECR must be tagged with the fully qualified ECR repository name.pFor more information about CodeBuild environment settings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref.html"Build Environment Reference for AWS CodeBuild/a/span.pFor more information about built-in CodeBuild standard images, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-available.html"Docker Images Provided by CodeBuild/a/span.pFor more information about CodeBuild environment variables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-env-vars.html"Environment Variables in Build Environments/a/span.pFor more information about how to push a Docker image to Amazon ECR, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/docker-push-ecr-image.html"Pushing a Docker Image/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up the CodeBuild project with the latest aws/codebuild/standard image. Specify the ECR repository as the output artifact. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to hold the current number for the build project. Increment and retrieve this number during each run of the build. Use Docker tag commands to tag the image with the build number.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeBuild does not support an ECR repository output artifact. CodeBuild can provide a simple incrementing version number with the CODEBUILD_BUILD_NUMBER variable. There is no need to track this number by using DynamoDB. Docker images that you push to Amazon ECR must be tagged with the fully qualified ECR repository name. You must push the resulting Docker image to the ECR repository.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up the CodeBuild project with the latest Java image. Specify the ECR repository as the output artifact. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to hold the current number for the build project. Increment and retrieve this number during each run of the build. Use Docker tag commands to tag the image with the fully qualified ECR repository name and build number.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Standard images that have Java and Docker preinstalled supersede CodeBuild language-specific images. CodeBuild does not support an ECR repository output artifact. CodeBuild can provide a simple incrementing version number with the CODEBUILD_BUILD_NUMBER variable. There is no need to track this number by using DynamoDB. You must push the resulting Docker image to the ECR repository.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up the CodeBuild project with the latest Java image. Specify an Amazon S3 bucket as the output artifact. Use the CODEBUILD_BUILD_NUMBER variable and Docker tag commands to tag the image with the build number. Use the Docker export command to produce a .tar file. Specify the .tar file in the artifacts or files section. Associate the CodeBuild project's S3 bucket with the ECR repository.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Standard images that have Java and Docker preinstalled supersede CodeBuild language-specific images. Docker images that you push to Amazon ECR must be tagged with the fully qualified ECR repository name. You cannot associate an S3 bucket with an ECR repository.

question_content: pA company has an Amazon S3 bucket that stores log data. The log data is a combination of AWS logs and custom logs from a variety of AWS sources and external sources. Most of the log data is in a JSON format, and some of the log data is in a CSV format. The S3 bucket receives new objects each night. Several of the external logs are sourced directly from customer systems.pA DevOps engineer needs to be able to directly analyze data from all the JSON logs each morning.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Create an AWS Glue crawler with an exclude pattern of *.csv. Schedule the AWS Glue crawler to run daily after the S3 bucket receives the new objects. Run Athena queries directly on the S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Athena does not recognize exclude patterns that are specified for an AWS Glue crawler. To ensure that Athena does not query the CSV objects, you should place the CSV objects in a different location.pFor more information about include patterns and exclude patterns, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/define-crawler.html#crawler-data-stores-exclude"Include and Exclude Patterns/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Create an AWS Glue crawler with an include pattern of *.json. Schedule the AWS Glue crawler to run daily after the S3 bucket receives the new objects. Run Athena queries directly on the S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Glue crawlers do not support include patterns. AWS Glue crawlers support only exclude patterns.pFor more information about include patterns and exclude patterns, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/define-crawler.html#crawler-data-stores-exclude"Include and Exclude Patterns/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second S3 bucket. Modify the sources of the log data to route CSV logs to the initial S3 bucket and to route JSON logs to the second S3 bucket. Configure the second S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Schedule an AWS Glue crawler to run daily on the second S3 bucket. Run Athena queries directly on the second S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Some of the external logs are sourced directly from customer systems. It might be difficult or impossible to modify these sources. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement of least implementation effort.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second S3 bucket. Schedule a daily S3 Batch Operations job to move the JSON objects to the second S3 bucket. Configure the second S3 bucket as a data source for Amazon Athena. Schedule an AWS Glue crawler to run daily on the second S3 bucket. Run Athena queries directly on the second S3 bucket to conduct the required analysis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Athena is an interactive query service that you can use to analyze data directly in S3 buckets by using standard SQL. AWS Glue crawlers provide the metadata for Athena. To ensure that Athena does not query the CSV objects, you can place the CSV objects in a different S3 bucket. The use of S3 Batch Operations to separate the JSON objects into their own S3 bucket requires the least implementation effort in this scenario.pFor more information about Athena, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html"What Is Amazon Athena?/a/spanpFor more information about AWS Glue crawlers in Athena, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/data-sources-glue.html"Using AWS Glue to Connect to Data Sources in Amazon S3/a/span.pFor more information about how to use S3 Batch Operations to copy objects, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/batch-ops-copy-object.html"Copy Objects/a/span.

question_content: pA company has converted all of its Amazon EC2 instances to use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) rather than IMDSv1. The company needs to implement a solution to enforce IMDSv2 for any EC2 instances that are launched or modified in the future to use IMDSv1.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pTurn on AWS Config. Create an AWS Config rule that detects whether EC2 instances are using IMDSv2. Set up an automatic remediation action to run an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to configure EC2 instances that are not using IMDSv2 to use IMDSv2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS Config rules can detect when EC2 instances are launched or changed. The ec2-imdsv2-check AWS Config rule can mark an EC2 instance NON_COMPLIANT if the HttpTokens parameter is set to optional. AWS Config rules can have automatic remediation actions that can invoke Systems Manager Automation runbooks. The AWSConfigRemediation-EnforceEC2InstanceIMDSv2 runbook can switch an EC2 instance to IMDSv2 by enforcing the use of HttpTokens.pFor more information about IMDSv2, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html"Use IMDSv2/a/span.pFor more information about AWS Config rules, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/evaluate-config.html"Evaluating Resources with AWS Config Rules/a/span.pFor more information about how to remediate noncompliant resources, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html#setup-autoremediation"Setting up Auto Remediation (Console)/a/span.pFor more information about the ec2-imdsv2-check AWS Config rule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ec2-imdsv2-check.html"ec2-imdsv2-check/a/span.pFor more information about Systems Manager Automation runbooks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-runbook-reference.html"Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor the EC2 RunInstances operation. Configure the EventBridge rule with AWS API Call via CloudTrail as the event type and EC2 as the AWS service. Specify as the target an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that configures EC2 instances to use IMDSv2.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This EventBridge rule could reliably detect whenever an EC2 instance is launched. However, this rule would not detect existing EC2 instances that have been modified to use IMDSv1 instead of IMDSv2.pFor more information about IMDSv2, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html"Use IMDSv2/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM policy to deny the EC2 RunInstances action if the MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required condition is not met. Attach this policy to all IAM roles that EC2 instances will use.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An IAM role that is attached to an EC2 instance does not apply to the principal that launched the EC2 instance. Therefore, the EC2 instance itself would not be restricted from using IMDSv1. Only software that is running on such an EC2 instance would be restricted from launching an EC2 instance that uses IMDSv1. Additionally, this solution would not prevent EC2 instances from being modified to use IMDSv1 after launch.pFor more information about IAM roles for EC2 instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html"IAM Roles for Amazon EC2/a/span.pFor more information about IMDSv2, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html"Use IMDSv2/a/span.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING lifecycle hook. Notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to call the EC2 ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions API operation to set the HttpTokens parameter to required.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Lifecycle hooks are a feature of Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling. EC2 instances that are launched independently of Auto Scaling groups would not be affected by lifecycle hooks. This solution also would not prevent EC2 instances from being modified to use IMDSv1 after launch.pFor more information about lifecycle hooks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html"Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling Lifecycle Hooks/a/span.
